`helper/src/gml.rs`:

```rs
//! GameMaker games (GameMaker Studio 2 before 2.3, bytecode games: their code and names are in
//! data.win or game.unx). Every instance, and the global object, keeps its variables in a hash
//! map at +0x58: {size (a power of two), used, mask = size - 1, grow threshold = 0.6 size,
//! elements}, elements of 16 bytes {RValue*, key, hash (0 = empty)}, the key being the
//! variable's id from the data file's VARI chunk + 100000. An RValue is 16 bytes {value, flags,
//! kind}: kind 0 a double, 7 an int32, 10 an int64 (Ferret's `gm` type reads whichever). An instance's id (100000 up) and object index (into the
//! OBJT chunk) sit side by side further in (+0xbc and +0xc4 on the runners seen; voted on). So a value is
//! named by its object and variable: `gml:global.totalmoney`, `gml:player1.hp` (every
//! instance of player1).

use crate::names::Heap;
use crate::ue::{Listed, ListedObject};
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
use crate::mem::Mem;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

/// Map keys are a variable's id plus this.
const KEY_BASE: u32 = 100000;
/// Where an instance's id and object index are looked for (from the map pointer's object).
const ID_FROM: u64 = 0x60;
const ID_TO: u64 = 0x200;
/// Largest variable map read.
const MAX_MAP: u32 = 1 << 16;
/// RValue kinds.
const REAL: u32 = 0;
const INT32: u32 = 7;
const INT64: u32 = 10;

/// What the game's data file names: objects by index, and which variables the game uses as
/// global ones (VARI's instance type -5; YYC builds have no VARI).
pub struct Names {
    globals: HashSet<String>,
    objects: Vec<String>,
}

fn u32_at(d: &[u8], o: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    d.get(o..o + 4).map(|b| u32::from_le_bytes(b.try_into().unwrap()))
}

fn cstr(d: &[u8], o: usize) -> Option<String> {
    let rest = d.get(o..)?;
    let end = rest.iter().position(|&b| b == 0)?;
    Some(String::from_utf8_lossy(&rest[..end]).into_owned())
}

impl Names {
    /// Reads OBJT (a list of offsets to {name, ...}) and VARI (bytecode 15 and later: a 12-byte
    /// header, then {name, instance type, id, occurrences, first use}).
    pub fn parse(d: &[u8]) -> Option<Names> {
        if d.get(..4) != Some(b"FORM") {
            return None;
        }
        let mut chunks: HashMap<&[u8], (usize, usize)> = HashMap::new();
        let mut i = 8;
        while i + 8 <= d.len() {
            let size = u32_at(d, i + 4)? as usize;
            chunks.insert(&d[i..i + 4], (i + 8, size));
            i += 8 + size;
        }
        let mut globals = HashSet::new();
        if let Some(&(vo, vs)) = chunks.get(&b"VARI"[..]) {
            let mut p = vo + 12;
            while p + 20 <= vo + vs {
                if u32_at(d, p + 4)? as i32 == -5 {
                    globals.extend(cstr(d, u32_at(d, p)? as usize));
                }
                p += 20;
            }
        }
        let (oo, _) = *chunks.get(&b"OBJT"[..])?;
        let n = u32_at(d, oo)? as usize;
        let objects = (0..n).map(|k| u32_at(d, oo + 4 + 4 * k).and_then(|e| cstr(d, u32_at(d, e as usize)? as usize)).unwrap_or_default()).collect();
        Some(Names { globals, objects })
    }
}

/// A variable's name the way the runner keeps it: a C string an array of slots points to
/// (map key - 100000), read from memory.
fn read_name(mem: &Mem, slots: u64, key: u32) -> Option<String> {
    let p = word(mem, slots + 8 * u64::from(key.checked_sub(KEY_BASE)?))?;
    let mut b = [0u8; 64];
    let n = mem.read_at(&mut b, p).ok()?;
    let end = b[..n].iter().position(|&c| c == 0)?;
    let t = std::str::from_utf8(&b[..end]).ok()?;
    (!t.is_empty() && t.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_' || c == '@')).then(|| t.to_owned())
}

/// The game's data file: next to the program, or in its assets folder.
pub fn data_file(pid: u32, program: Option<&Path>) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let dir = program?.parent()?;
    let inside = crate::os::inside(pid, dir);
    ["data.win", "game.unx", "assets/game.unx"].iter().map(|f| inside.join(f)).find(|p| p.exists())
}

/// An owner of a variable map: the global object or an instance.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct Owner {
    addr: u64,
    /// The variable map's header.
    map: u64,
    /// Instance id and object index; None for the global object.
    instance: Option<(u32, u32)>,
}

/// The located objects of one game (per run).
pub struct Gml {
    names: Names,
    /// The runner's array of variable names by slot (a map key - 100000).
    slots: u64,
    /// The names of the keys seen when located (others are read when asked for).
    known: HashMap<u32, String>,
    /// Where an instance's id is, from its start (the object index follows).
    id_at: u64,
    /// Instances' C++ vtable.
    class: u64,
    owners: Vec<Owner>,
    /// Maps found, for `gml` (diagnostics).
    maps: usize,
}

fn word(mem: &Mem, at: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    let mut b = [0u8; 8];
    mem.read_exact_at(&mut b, at).ok().map(|_| u64::from_le_bytes(b))
}

fn half(mem: &Mem, at: u64) -> Option<u32> {
    let mut b = [0u8; 4];
    mem.read_exact_at(&mut b, at).ok().map(|_| u32::from_le_bytes(b))
}

/// A map's entries: (RValue address, key), read from its header.
fn entries(mem: &Mem, map: u64) -> Option<Vec<(u64, u32)>> {
    let mut h = [0u8; 24];
    mem.read_exact_at(&mut h, map).ok()?;
    let (size, used, mask, grow) = (u32_at(&h, 0)?, u32_at(&h, 4)?, u32_at(&h, 8)?, u32_at(&h, 12)?);
    if size < 8 || size > MAX_MAP || size & (size - 1) != 0 || mask != size - 1 || grow != size * 6 / 10 || used == 0 || used > size {
        return None;
    }
    let el = u64::from_le_bytes(h[16..24].try_into().unwrap());
    let mut b = vec![0u8; 16 * size as usize];
    mem.read_exact_at(&mut b, el).ok()?;
    let out: Vec<(u64, u32)> = b
        .chunks(16)
        .filter(|e| u32_at(e, 12) != Some(0))
        .map(|e| (u64::from_le_bytes(e[..8].try_into().unwrap()), u32_at(e, 8).unwrap_or(0)))
        .collect();
    (out.len() == used as usize).then_some(out)
}

impl Gml {
    /// Finds the variable maps (their headers, in one pass with the runtime's first two
    /// variables' names, "prototype" and "@@array@@"), their owners and the array of variable
    /// names pointing to those names (a second pass), and where instances keep their id (a vote).
    fn locate(heap: &Heap, names: Names) -> Option<Gml> {
        if heap.width() != 8 {
            return None;
        }
        let mem = heap.mem();
        let mut heads = Vec::new();
        let (mut first, mut second) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        heap.each_chunk(24, |addr, b, fresh| {
            for off in (0..fresh).step_by(8) {
                let Some(h) = b.get(off..off + 16) else { break };
                let (size, mask) = (u32_at(h, 0).unwrap(), u32_at(h, 8).unwrap());
                if mask.wrapping_add(1) != size || size < 8 || size > MAX_MAP || size & mask != 0 || u32_at(h, 12) != Some(size * 6 / 10) {
                    continue;
                }
                heads.push(addr + off as u64);
            }
            for i in 0..fresh.min(b.len().saturating_sub(10)) {
                match b[i] {
                    b'p' if &b[i..i + 10] == b"prototype\0" => first.push(addr + i as u64),
                    b'@' if &b[i..i + 10] == b"@@array@@\0" => second.push(addr + i as u64),
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
        });
        // Maps keyed by variables only (their names are checked once the names are found).
        let in_range = |k: u32| k >= KEY_BASE && k - KEY_BASE < MAX_MAP;
        let heads: Vec<(u64, Vec<(u64, u32)>)> =
            heads.into_iter().filter_map(|h| Some((h, entries(mem, h).filter(|e| e.iter().all(|&(_, k)| in_range(k)))?))).collect();
        let targets: Vec<u64> = heads.iter().map(|(h, _)| *h).chain(first.iter().copied()).collect();
        let refs = heap.referrers(&targets);
        let slots = refs.iter().copied().find(|&r| word(mem, r).is_some_and(|w| first.contains(&w)) && word(mem, r + 8).is_some_and(|w| second.contains(&w)))?;
        let mut known: HashMap<u32, String> = HashMap::new();
        let mut name_of = |k: u32| -> bool {
            if known.contains_key(&k) {
                return true;
            }
            match read_name(mem, slots, k) {
                Some(n) => {
                    known.insert(k, n);
                    true
                }
                None => false,
            }
        };
        let mut maps = HashMap::new();
        for (h, e) in &heads {
            if e.iter().all(|&(_, k)| name_of(k)) {
                maps.insert(*h, ());
            }
        }
        let objects = names.objects.len() as u32;
        let valid = |a: u64, at: u64| {
            let (Some(id), Some(obj)) = (half(mem, a + at), half(mem, a + at + 4)) else { return false };
            (KEY_BASE..100_000_000).contains(&id) && obj < objects
        };
        let candidates: Vec<(u64, u64)> =
            refs.iter().filter_map(|&r| Some((r.checked_sub(0x58)?, word(mem, r).filter(|m| maps.contains_key(m))?))).collect();
        // Instances are of one C++ class (one vtable): the class and offset where (nearly) all
        // its objects hold an id and an object index, all different, the most of them (a constant pair
        // passes the checks too: Zordak's renderers all had 0xffffff, 0 at +0x90), then the
        // smallest (ids count up from 100000). Voting over every owner let thousands of the
        // runtime's own objects outvote Dunkehr's few instances at its title (+0x138, not +0xbc).
        let mut classes: HashMap<u64, Vec<u64>> = HashMap::new();
        for &(o, _) in &candidates {
            if let Some(vt) = word(mem, o) {
                classes.entry(vt).or_default().push(o);
            }
        }
        let mut best: Option<((usize, std::cmp::Reverse<u32>), u64, u64)> = None;
        for (vt, members) in &classes {
            for at in (ID_FROM..ID_TO).step_by(4) {
                let mut ids: Vec<u32> = members.iter().filter(|&&o| valid(o, at)).filter_map(|&o| half(mem, o + at)).collect();
                if ids.len() * 10 < members.len() * 9 {
                    continue;
                }
                let found = ids.len();
                ids.sort_unstable();
                ids.dedup();
                // No two instances share an id (Dunkehr's array objects held 3 values at +0x138).
                if ids.len() * 10 < found * 9 {
                    continue;
                }
                let score = (ids.len(), std::cmp::Reverse(ids.last().copied().unwrap_or(u32::MAX)));
                if best.as_ref().is_none_or(|(b, _, _)| score > *b) {
                    best = Some((score, *vt, at));
                }
            }
        }
        let (_, class, id_at) = best?;
        let owners: Vec<Owner> = candidates
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(addr, map)| {
                let ok = word(mem, addr) == Some(class) && valid(addr, id_at);
                let instance = ok.then(|| (half(mem, addr + id_at).unwrap_or(0), half(mem, addr + id_at + 4).unwrap_or(0)));
                Owner { addr, map, instance }
            })
            .collect();
        Some(Gml { names, slots, known, id_at, class, owners, maps: maps.len() })
    }

    fn name(&self, mem: &Mem, key: u32) -> Option<String> {
        self.known.get(&key).cloned().or_else(|| read_name(mem, self.slots, key))
    }

    /// The key of a variable by name (a slot of the runner's array).
    fn key_of(&self, mem: &Mem, name: &str) -> Option<u32> {
        if let Some((k, _)) = self.known.iter().find(|(_, n)| *n == name) {
            return Some(*k);
        }
        (KEY_BASE..KEY_BASE + MAX_MAP).take_while(|&k| word(mem, self.slots + 8 * u64::from(k - KEY_BASE)).is_some()).find(|&k| read_name(mem, self.slots, k).as_deref() == Some(name))
    }

    /// The global object: of the owners that aren't instances, the one holding the most of the
    /// game's global variables (by VARI), or the most variables.
    fn global(&self, mem: &Mem) -> Option<&Owner> {
        self.owners.iter().filter(|o| o.instance.is_none()).max_by_key(|o| {
            let e = entries(mem, o.map).unwrap_or_default();
            (e.iter().filter(|&&(_, k)| self.name(mem, k).is_some_and(|n| self.names.globals.contains(&n))).count(), e.len())
        })
    }

    /// An owner's numbers: (variable name, address, kind).
    fn numbers(&self, mem: &Mem, o: &Owner) -> Vec<(String, u64, &'static str)> {
        let mut out: Vec<(String, u64, &'static str)> = entries(mem, o.map)
            .unwrap_or_default()
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|&(rv, _)| holds_number(mem, rv))
            .filter_map(|(rv, key)| Some((self.name(mem, key)?, rv, "gm")))
            .collect();
        out.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));
        out
    }

    fn object_name(&self, index: u32) -> String {
        self.names.objects.get(index as usize).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| format!("object {index}"))
    }
}

/// The number an RValue's 16 bytes hold: a double, an int32 or an int64; None for others
/// (strings, arrays, undefined).
pub fn rvalue_number(b: &[u8]) -> Option<f64> {
    let v = b.get(..8)?;
    match u32_at(b, 12)? & 0xff_ffff {
        REAL => Some(f64::from_le_bytes(v.try_into().unwrap())).filter(|x| x.is_finite()),
        INT32 => Some(i32::from_le_bytes(v[..4].try_into().unwrap()) as f64),
        INT64 => Some(i64::from_le_bytes(v.try_into().unwrap()) as f64),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Whether an RValue holds a number now.
fn holds_number(mem: &Mem, rv: u64) -> bool {
    let mut b = [0u8; 16];
    mem.read_exact_at(&mut b, rv).is_ok() && rvalue_number(&b).is_some()
}

/// The game attached to, located; searched again when asked for after `REFRESH` (instances
/// come and go with rooms).
pub fn shared(heap: &Heap, program: Option<&Path>, fresh: bool) -> Option<Arc<Gml>> {
    const REFRESH: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
    static FOUND: Mutex<Option<(u32, Arc<Gml>, Instant)>> = Mutex::new(None);
    let mut found = FOUND.lock().unwrap();
    if let Some((pid, g, at)) = found.as_ref() {
        if *pid == heap.pid && (!fresh || at.elapsed() < REFRESH) {
            return Some(g.clone());
        }
    }
    let data = std::fs::read(data_file(heap.pid, program)?).ok()?;
    let g = Arc::new(Gml::locate(heap, Names::parse(&data)?)?);
    *found = Some((heap.pid, g.clone(), Instant::now()));
    Some(g)
}

/// A saved path: the global object's or an object's instances' variable.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct GmlPath {
    /// None for global.
    object: Option<String>,
    var: String,
}

impl GmlPath {
    pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Option<GmlPath> {
        let (object, var) = text.strip_prefix("gml:")?.rsplit_once('.')?;
        let ok = |s: &str| !s.is_empty() && s.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_');
        if !ok(object) || !ok(var) {
            return None;
        }
        Some(GmlPath { object: (object != "global").then(|| object.to_owned()), var: var.to_owned() })
    }

    pub fn text(&self) -> String {
        format!("gml:{}.{}", self.object.as_deref().unwrap_or("global"), self.var)
    }

    pub fn describe(&self) -> String {
        match &self.object {
            Some(o) => format!("{} of every {o}", self.var),
            None => format!("global.{}", self.var),
        }
    }
}

/// The global object or the instances the path starts from.
pub fn find_roots(heap: &Heap, program: Option<&Path>, path: &GmlPath) -> Vec<u64> {
    let Some(g) = shared(heap, program, true) else { return Vec::new() };
    let mem = heap.mem();
    match &path.object {
        None => g.global(mem).map(|o| vec![o.addr]).unwrap_or_default(),
        Some(name) => {
            let index = g.names.objects.iter().position(|o| o == name);
            g.owners.iter().filter(|o| o.instance.is_some_and(|(_, obj)| Some(obj as usize) == index)).map(|o| o.addr).collect()
        }
    }
}

/// Where the variable is in each root that still is what it was (an instance of the object,
/// the global object holding the variable): the RValue's value, while it holds a number.
pub fn walk(heap: &Heap, program: Option<&Path>, roots: &[u64], path: &GmlPath) -> Vec<u64> {
    let Some(g) = shared(heap, program, false) else { return Vec::new() };
    let mem = heap.mem();
    let Some(key) = g.key_of(mem, &path.var) else { return Vec::new() };
    let index = path.object.as_ref().and_then(|n| g.names.objects.iter().position(|o| o == n));
    roots
        .iter()
        .filter(|&&r| match index {
            Some(i) => word(mem, r) == Some(g.class) && half(mem, r + g.id_at).is_some_and(|id| id >= KEY_BASE) && half(mem, r + g.id_at + 4) == Some(i as u32),
            None => path.object.is_none(),
        })
        .filter_map(|&r| {
            let map = word(mem, r + 0x58)?;
            let rv = entries(mem, map)?.into_iter().find(|&(_, k)| k == key)?.0;
            holds_number(mem, rv).then_some(rv)
        })
        .collect()
}

/// The path to a number some instance's or the global object's variable holds.
pub fn discover(heap: &Heap, program: Option<&Path>, target: u64) -> Option<(GmlPath, Vec<u64>)> {
    let g = shared(heap, program, true)?;
    let mem = heap.mem();
    let global = g.global(mem).map(|o| o.addr);
    for o in &g.owners {
        if o.instance.is_none() && Some(o.addr) != global {
            continue;
        }
        let Some((rv, key)) = entries(mem, o.map).unwrap_or_default().into_iter().find(|&(rv, _)| rv == target) else { continue };
        let Some(var) = g.name(mem, key).filter(|_| holds_number(mem, rv)) else { continue };
        let object = o.instance.map(|(_, obj)| g.object_name(obj));
        let path = GmlPath { object, var };
        let leads = walk(heap, program, &find_roots(heap, program, &path), &path);
        if leads.contains(&rv) {
            return Some((path, leads));
        }
    }
    None
}

/// The Browse tab's list: the global variables, then every instance's numbers (the player's
/// objects by name in the main list).
pub fn player(heap: &Heap, program: Option<&Path>) -> Option<Vec<ListedObject>> {
    let g = shared(heap, program, true)?;
    let mem = heap.mem();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    if let Some(o) = g.global(mem) {
        let fields = g.numbers(mem, o).into_iter().map(|(label, addr, kind)| Listed { label, addr, kind }).collect();
        out.push(ListedObject { name: "@global".into(), class: "global".into(), role: "game", owner: None, more: false, fields });
    }
    let mut instances: Vec<&Owner> = g.owners.iter().filter(|o| o.instance.is_some()).collect();
    instances.sort_by_key(|o| o.instance);
    let mut listed = 0;
    for o in instances {
        let (id, obj) = o.instance.unwrap_or_default();
        let class = g.object_name(obj);
        let fields: Vec<Listed> = g.numbers(mem, o).into_iter().map(|(label, addr, kind)| Listed { label, addr, kind }).collect();
        if fields.is_empty() || listed > crate::ue::MAX_LISTED {
            continue;
        }
        listed += fields.len();
        let main = crate::mono::player_like(&class);
        out.push(ListedObject { name: format!("{class} ({id})"), class, role: if main { "character" } else { "game" }, owner: None, more: !main, fields });
    }
    out.sort_by_key(|o| (o.more, o.role != "character"));
    Some(out)
}

/// gml: what was found (maps, owners, the id offset, the global object).
pub fn diagnose(heap: &Heap, program: Option<&Path>) -> Vec<String> {
    let Some(path) = data_file(heap.pid, program) else { return vec!["no data.win or game.unx next to the program".into()] };
    let Ok(data) = std::fs::read(&path) else { return vec![format!("can't read {}", path.display())] };
    let Some(names) = Names::parse(&data) else { return vec![format!("{}: no OBJT chunk", path.display())] };
    let mut lines = vec![format!("{}: {} global variable names, {} objects", path.display(), names.globals.len(), names.objects.len())];
    // Every map header, valid keys or not: the biggest, with their key ranges.
    let mem = heap.mem();
    let mut all: Vec<(u64, Vec<(u64, u32)>)> = Vec::new();
    heap.each_chunk(24, |addr, b, fresh| {
        for off in (0..fresh).step_by(8) {
            let Some(h) = b.get(off..off + 16) else { break };
            let (size, mask) = (u32_at(h, 0).unwrap(), u32_at(h, 8).unwrap());
            if mask.wrapping_add(1) == size && size >= 64 && size <= MAX_MAP && size & mask == 0 && u32_at(h, 12) == Some(size * 6 / 10) {
                if let Some(e) = entries(mem, addr + off as u64) {
                    all.push((addr + off as u64, e));
                }
            }
        }
    });
    all.sort_by_key(|(_, e)| std::cmp::Reverse(e.len()));
    for (h, e) in all.iter().take(12) {
        let (lo, hi) = (e.iter().map(|x| x.1).min().unwrap_or(0), e.iter().map(|x| x.1).max().unwrap_or(0));
        lines.push(format!("map 0x{h:x}: {} keys {lo}..{hi}", e.len()));
    }
    let Some(g) = shared(heap, program, true) else {
        lines.push("no variable maps found".into());
        return lines;
    };
    let instances = g.owners.iter().filter(|o| o.instance.is_some()).count();
    lines.push(format!("{} maps, {} owners, {instances} instances, id at +0x{:x}, names at 0x{:x}", g.maps, g.owners.len(), g.id_at, g.slots));
    for o in g.owners.iter().filter(|o| o.instance.is_some()).take(15) {
        let (id, obj) = o.instance.unwrap_or_default();
        let nums = g.numbers(mem, o);
        let sample: Vec<String> = nums
            .iter()
            .take(6)
            .map(|(n, a, _)| {
                let mut b = [0u8; 16];
                let v = mem.read_exact_at(&mut b, *a).ok().and_then(|_| rvalue_number(&b));
                format!("{n}={}", v.unwrap_or(f64::NAN))
            })
            .collect();
        lines.push(format!("  {} ({id}) at 0x{:x}: {}", g.object_name(obj), o.addr, sample.join(", ")));
    }
    if let Some(o) = g.global(mem) {
        lines.push(format!("global object 0x{:x}: {} numbers", o.addr, g.numbers(mem, o).len()));
    }
    lines
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {

    }
}
```

`helper/src/godot.rs`:

```rs
// Godot dictionaries: a value kept as an entry of a Dictionary the game's scripts fill
// (Lumencraft's inventory stacks are {"id": 0, "amount": 2, "data": null, "index": 6}). The
// game re-creates such entries as it runs, in memory allocated at run time, so neither code
// patterns (the GDScript interpreter is shared code) nor pointer paths find them again; their
// keys do.
// Memory (64-bit Linux builds): a Dictionary keeps its entries in a list whose elements are
// { const Variant *key; Variant value; Element *next, *prev; void *list }, a Variant is
// { u32 type; 4 bytes of padding (not always zero); 16 bytes of data }, type 2 = int (an int64),
// 3 = real (a double),
// 4 = String (data = pointer to its characters, UTF-32: wchar_t is 4 bytes on Linux).
// Godot 4 keeps the entries in a HashMap whose elements are { Element *next, *prev; Variant key;
// Variant value }, in insertion order; keys are Strings (4) or StringNames (21: data = pointer
// to { u32 refcount, u32 static count, then its String at +8 (4.5+), else a C string there and
// the String at +0x10 }). Strings are UTF-32 on every platform.
// Text form: {amount|id=0,index} = the "amount" entry of every dictionary that also has an
// "id" entry holding 0 and an "index" entry.

use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use crate::mem::Mem;
use std::sync::Mutex;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use crate::names::Heap;

const INT: u32 = 2;
const REAL: u32 = 3;
const STRING: u32 = 4;
const STRING_NAME: u32 = 21;
/// Bytes of an element read when searching memory.
const ELEMENT: usize = 0x38;
const MAX_KEY: usize = 64;
/// Entries per dictionary followed: a misread link can't make a walk take forever.
const MAX_ENTRIES: usize = 64;
/// A path leading to more places than this is too loose to write through.
const MAX_PLACES: usize = 16;
/// How long the elements a search found serve other searches.
const FOUND_FOR: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);
/// How long a key that was looked for is looked for by every search.
const WANTED_FOR: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);

/// The last search's elements by key. Saved values of a game mostly share their key (every
/// Lumencraft stack is "amount"), and the limits and the window each look for a missing one:
/// each search was a pass over the game's memory (~1-2 s on 2.2 GB) of its own.
struct Found {
    pid: u32,
    at: Instant,
    by_key: HashMap<String, Vec<u64>>,
}

static FOUND: Mutex<Option<Found>> = Mutex::new(None);
/// Keys looked for lately (pid, key, when): one search looks for all of them.
static WANTED: Mutex<Vec<(u32, String, Instant)>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct DictPath {
    key: String,
    /// The dictionary's other entries: the key, and the int it must hold when given.
    with: Vec<(String, Option<i64>)>,
}

/// Keys go into the text as they are: only those that keep a path one word.
fn good_key(k: &str) -> bool {
    !k.is_empty() && k.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_')
}

impl DictPath {
    pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        let inner = text.strip_prefix('{')?.strip_suffix('}')?;
        let (key, rest) = inner.split_once('|').unwrap_or((inner, ""));
        let mut with = Vec::new();
        for w in rest.split(',').filter(|w| !w.is_empty()) {
            let (k, v) = match w.split_once('=') {
                Some((k, v)) => (k, Some(v.parse().ok()?)),
                None => (w, None),
            };
            if !good_key(k) {
                return None;
            }
            with.push((k.to_owned(), v));
        }
        good_key(key).then(|| DictPath { key: key.to_owned(), with })
    }

    pub fn text(&self) -> String {
        let with: Vec<String> = self
            .with
            .iter()
            .map(|(k, v)| match v {
                Some(v) => format!("{k}={v}"),
                None => k.clone(),
            })
            .collect();
        format!("{{{}|{}}}", self.key, with.join(","))
    }

    /// The same path whatever slot the item is in.
    fn any_slot(&self) -> DictPath {
        let with = self.with.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), if slot_key(k) { None } else { *v })).collect();
        DictPath { key: self.key.clone(), with }
    }

    fn has_slot(&self) -> bool {
        self.with.iter().any(|(k, v)| v.is_some() && slot_key(k))
    }

    /// In words: ""amount" where "id" is 0".
    pub fn describe(&self) -> String {
        let held: Vec<String> = self.with.iter().filter_map(|(k, v)| Some(format!("\"{k}\" is {}", (*v)?))).collect();
        match held.is_empty() {
            true => format!("\"{}\" in the game's dictionaries", self.key),
            false => format!("\"{}\" where {}", self.key, held.join(" and ")),
        }
    }
}

/// How a dictionary's elements are laid out.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
enum Shape {
    V3,
    V4,
}

const SHAPES: [Shape; 2] = [Shape::V3, Shape::V4];

impl Shape {
    /// Offsets in an element: the value's data, the links.
    fn value(self) -> u64 {
        match self {
            Shape::V3 => 16,
            Shape::V4 => 0x30,
        }
    }

    fn next(self) -> u64 {
        match self {
            Shape::V3 => 32,
            Shape::V4 => 0,
        }
    }

    fn prev(self) -> u64 {
        match self {
            Shape::V3 => 40,
            Shape::V4 => 8,
        }
    }
}

/// Reads the game's dictionaries; keys are cached by the address of their characters (a key's
/// text is shared by every dictionary that has it).
struct Dicts<'a> {
    heap: &'a Heap<'a>,
    keys: RefCell<HashMap<u64, Option<String>>>,
}

impl<'a> Dicts<'a> {
    fn new(heap: &'a Heap<'a>) -> Self {
        Dicts { heap, keys: RefCell::default() }
    }

    fn mem(&self) -> &Mem {
        self.heap.mem()
    }

    fn u32_at(&self, at: u64) -> Option<u32> {
        let mut b = [0u8; 4];
        self.mem().read_exact_at(&mut b, at).ok()?;
        Some(u32::from_le_bytes(b))
    }

    fn u64_at(&self, at: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        let mut b = [0u8; 8];
        self.mem().read_exact_at(&mut b, at).ok()?;
        Some(u64::from_le_bytes(b))
    }

    fn link(&self, p: u64) -> bool {
        p == 0 || self.heap.is_pointer(p)
    }

    /// Looks like an element with a number for its value (checked on the words already read):
    /// `key` is the key's pointer (Godot 3) or its Variant type (Godot 4).
    fn shaped(&self, shape: Shape, key: u64, value_type: u32, next: u64, prev: u64) -> bool {
        let key_ok = match shape {
            Shape::V3 => self.heap.is_pointer(key),
            Shape::V4 => key == STRING as u64 || key == STRING_NAME as u64,
        };
        (value_type == INT || value_type == REAL) && key_ok && (next != 0 || prev != 0) && self.link(next) && self.link(prev)
    }

    fn is(&self, e: u64, shape: Shape) -> bool {
        let key = match shape {
            Shape::V3 => self.u64_at(e),
            Shape::V4 => self.u32_at(e + 0x10).map(u64::from),
        };
        let (Some(key), Some(t), Some(next), Some(prev)) =
            (key, self.u32_at(e + shape.value() - 8), self.u64_at(e + shape.next()), self.u64_at(e + shape.prev()))
        else {
            return false;
        };
        self.shaped(shape, key, t, next, prev)
    }

    /// The shape of the element at `e`, when it is one.
    fn element(&self, e: u64) -> Option<Shape> {
        SHAPES.into_iter().find(|&shape| self.is(e, shape))
    }

    /// The text of the String or StringName key of the element at `e`.
    fn key(&self, e: u64, shape: Shape) -> Option<String> {
        let k = match shape {
            Shape::V3 => self.u64_at(e)?,
            Shape::V4 => e + 0x10,
        };
        let chars = match self.u32_at(k)? {
            STRING => self.u64_at(k + 8)?,
            STRING_NAME if shape == Shape::V4 => {
                let sn = self.u64_at(k + 8).filter(|&p| self.heap.is_pointer(p))?;
                return [8, 0x10].into_iter().find_map(|at| self.u64_at(sn + at).filter(|&p| self.heap.is_pointer(p)).and_then(|c| self.chars(c)));
            }
            _ => return None,
        };
        self.chars(chars)
    }

    /// A key's UTF-32 characters at `chars`.
    fn chars(&self, chars: u64) -> Option<String> {
        if let Some(cached) = self.keys.borrow().get(&chars) {
            return cached.clone();
        }
        let mut b = [0u8; 4 * MAX_KEY];
        let text = self.mem().read_exact_at(&mut b, chars).ok().and_then(|_| {
            let units: Vec<u32> = b.chunks(4).map(|c| u32::from_le_bytes([c[0], c[1], c[2], c[3]])).take_while(|&c| c != 0).collect();
            let t: String = units.iter().map(|&c| char::from_u32(c)).collect::<Option<_>>()?;
            (units.len() < MAX_KEY && good_key(&t)).then_some(t)
        });
        self.keys.borrow_mut().insert(chars, text.clone());
        text
    }

    /// The element's number, int or real.
    fn number(&self, e: u64, shape: Shape) -> Option<f64> {
        match self.u32_at(e + shape.value() - 8)? {
            INT => self.int(e, shape).map(|v| v as f64),
            REAL => self.u64_at(e + shape.value()).map(f64::from_bits),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The slot the element's dictionary is in, when it has a slot key.
    fn slot(&self, e: u64, shape: Shape) -> Option<i64> {
        self.siblings(e, shape).into_iter().find(|(k, v)| v.is_some() && slot_key(k))?.1
    }

    fn int(&self, e: u64, shape: Shape) -> Option<i64> {
        (self.u32_at(e + shape.value() - 8)? == INT).then(|| self.u64_at(e + shape.value()).map(|v| v as i64)).flatten()
    }

    /// The other entries of the dictionary the element at `e` is in: their keys and ints.
    fn siblings(&self, e: u64, shape: Shape) -> Vec<(String, Option<i64>)> {
        let mut first = e;
        for _ in 0..MAX_ENTRIES {
            match self.u64_at(first + shape.prev()) {
                Some(p) if p != 0 && p != e && self.heap.is_pointer(p) => first = p,
                _ => break,
            }
        }
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let mut at = first;
        for _ in 0..MAX_ENTRIES {
            if at != e {
                if let Some(k) = self.key(at, shape) {
                    out.push((k, self.int(at, shape)));
                }
            }
            match self.u64_at(at + shape.next()) {
                Some(n) if n != 0 && n != first && self.heap.is_pointer(n) => at = n,
                _ => break,
            }
        }
        out
    }

    fn fits(&self, e: u64, path: &DictPath) -> bool {
        let Some(shape) = self.element(e) else { return false };
        if self.key(e, shape).as_deref() != Some(path.key.as_str()) {
            return false;
        }
        let siblings = self.siblings(e, shape);
        path.with.iter().all(|(k, v)| siblings.iter().any(|(sk, sv)| sk == k && (v.is_none() || sv == v)))
    }

    /// Every element in memory whose key is `key`, of either shape (one pass over the game's
    /// memory).
    fn with_key(&self, key: &str) -> Vec<u64> {
        self.with_keys(&[key.to_owned()]).remove(key).unwrap_or_default()
    }

    /// Every element in memory whose key is one of `keys`, by key: one pass for all of them.
    fn with_keys(&self, keys: &[String]) -> HashMap<String, Vec<u64>> {
        let mut found: HashMap<String, Vec<u64>> = HashMap::new();
        let word = |b: &[u8], o: usize| u64::from_le_bytes(b[o..o + 8].try_into().unwrap());
        let half = |b: &[u8], o: usize| u32::from_le_bytes(b[o..o + 4].try_into().unwrap());
        self.heap.each_chunk(ELEMENT, |addr, b, fresh| {
            for o in (0..fresh).step_by(8).take_while(|o| o + ELEMENT <= b.len()) {
                let e = addr + o as u64;
                for shape in SHAPES {
                    let t = half(b, o + shape.value() as usize - 8);
                    if t != INT && t != REAL {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let k = match shape {
                        Shape::V3 => word(b, o),
                        Shape::V4 => half(b, o + 0x10) as u64,
                    };
                    let (next, prev) = (word(b, o + shape.next() as usize), word(b, o + shape.prev() as usize));
                    if !self.shaped(shape, k, t, next, prev) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    if let Some(key) = self.key(e, shape).filter(|k| keys.contains(k)) {
                        found.entry(key).or_default().push(e);
                    }
                }
            }
        });
        found
    }

    /// Elements with `key`, from a search of the last few seconds when there was one (it looked
    /// for every key wanted lately), else from a new one. One search at a time: a second one
    /// waits and takes the first's result.
    fn recent_with_key(&self, key: &str) -> Vec<u64> {
        let pid = self.heap.pid;
        let wanted: Vec<String> = {
            let mut w = WANTED.lock().unwrap();
            w.retain(|(p, k, at)| *p == pid && at.elapsed() < WANTED_FOR && k != key);
            w.push((pid, key.to_owned(), Instant::now()));
            w.iter().map(|(_, k, _)| k.clone()).collect()
        };
        let mut found = FOUND.lock().unwrap();
        if let Some(f) = found.as_ref().filter(|f| f.pid == pid && f.at.elapsed() < FOUND_FOR) {
            if let Some(elements) = f.by_key.get(key) {
                return elements.clone();
            }
        }
        let by_key = self.with_keys(&wanted);
        let elements = by_key.get(key).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        *found = Some(Found { pid, at: Instant::now(), by_key: wanted.iter().map(|k| (k.clone(), by_key.get(k).cloned().unwrap_or_default())).collect() });
        elements
    }
}

/// The value's address of each element.
fn values(d: &Dicts, elements: &[u64]) -> Vec<u64> {
    elements.iter().filter_map(|&e| Some(e + d.element(e)?.value())).collect()
}

/// Elements the path leads to, among those found before (cheap: no search). A stack found
/// stays followed when the player moves it to another slot.
pub fn walk(heap: &Heap, roots: &[u64], path: &DictPath) -> Vec<u64> {
    let d = Dicts::new(heap);
    let path = path.any_slot();
    values(&d, &roots.iter().copied().filter(|&e| d.fits(e, &path)).collect::<Vec<_>>())
}

/// Searches the game's memory for the path's elements (the roots `walk` takes). The slot saved
/// is a preference: the game picks slots by pickup order, so on another map the item is
/// elsewhere (Lumencraft's iron: saved in slot 1, then in 7); then its biggest stack (a full
/// stack in the backpack rather than the one that overflowed onto the hotbar), with its copies.
pub fn find_roots(heap: &Heap, path: &DictPath) -> Vec<u64> {
    let d = Dicts::new(heap);
    let any = path.any_slot();
    let all: Vec<u64> = d.recent_with_key(&path.key).into_iter().filter(|&e| d.fits(e, &any)).collect();
    let mut found: Vec<u64> = all.iter().copied().filter(|&e| d.fits(e, path)).collect();
    if found.is_empty() && path.has_slot() {
        let stacks: Vec<(u64, Option<i64>, f64)> = all
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|&e| {
                let shape = d.element(e)?;
                Some((e, d.slot(e, shape), d.number(e, shape)?))
            })
            .collect();
        let biggest = stacks.iter().max_by(|a, b| a.2.total_cmp(&b.2)).map(|s| s.1);
        found = stacks.iter().filter(|s| Some(s.1) == biggest).map(|s| s.0).collect();
    }
    found.truncate(MAX_PLACES);
    found
}

/// A path to the value at `target` when it is an entry of a dictionary: its key, the other
/// keys of its dictionary, and the int of one of them: an "id" when there is one, else the one
/// that picks out the fewest dictionaries; plus the slot it is in when it is in one: an item can have several stacks,
/// and the game shows their total (Lumencraft: 200 lumen in the backpack, 1 on the hotbar; a
/// limit holding every stack at once let pickups and purchases go to the other one). The
/// player keeps the item in that slot. With the places it leads to now.
pub fn discover(heap: &Heap, target: u64) -> Option<(DictPath, Vec<u64>)> {
    let d = Dicts::new(heap);
    let (e, shape) = at_value(&d, target)?;
    let key = d.key(e, shape)?;
    let siblings = d.siblings(e, shape);
    if siblings.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let base = DictPath { key: key.clone(), with: siblings.iter().map(|(k, _)| (k.clone(), None)).collect() };
    let all: Vec<u64> = d.with_key(&key).into_iter().filter(|&x| d.fits(x, &base)).collect();
    let mut options = vec![base.clone()];
    // A slot alone would write to whatever the player puts there: it only narrows an item down.
    for (k, v) in siblings.iter().filter(|(k, v)| v.is_some() && !slot_key(k)) {
        let mut p = base.clone();
        p.with.iter_mut().filter(|(pk, _)| pk == k).for_each(|w| w.1 = *v);
        options.push(p);
    }
    let identity = |p: &DictPath| if p.with.iter().any(|(k, v)| v.is_some() && identity_key(k)) { 0 } else { 1 };
    options
        .into_iter()
        .map(|p| {
            let leads: Vec<u64> = all.iter().copied().filter(|&x| d.fits(x, &p)).collect();
            (p, leads)
        })
        .filter(|(_, leads)| leads.contains(&e) && leads.len() <= MAX_PLACES)
        .min_by_key(|(p, leads)| (identity(p), leads.len(), p.with.iter().filter(|w| w.1.is_some()).count()))
        .map(|(mut p, mut leads)| {
            let slot = siblings.iter().find(|(k, v)| v.is_some() && slot_key(k));
            if let Some((k, v)) = slot.filter(|_| identity(&p) == 0) {
                p.with.iter_mut().filter(|(pk, _)| pk == k).for_each(|w| w.1 = *v);
                leads.retain(|&x| d.fits(x, &p));
            }
            (p, values(&d, &leads))
        })
}

/// The element whose value is at `addr`, and its shape.
fn at_value(d: &Dicts, addr: u64) -> Option<(u64, Shape)> {
    SHAPES.into_iter().find_map(|shape| {
        let e = addr.checked_sub(shape.value())?;
        d.is(e, shape).then_some((e, shape))
    })
}

/// What the value at `addr` is, when it is an entry of a dictionary: its key, and the ids of
/// its dictionary (""amount" where "id" is 0"), for telling an inventory stack from a statistic
/// among a search's matches.
pub fn about(heap: &Heap, addr: u64) -> Option<String> {
    let d = Dicts::new(heap);
    let (e, shape) = at_value(&d, addr)?;
    let key = d.key(e, shape)?;
    let ids: Vec<String> = d
        .siblings(e, shape)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|(k, v)| v.is_some() && (identity_key(k) || slot_key(k)))
        .map(|(k, v)| format!("\"{k}\" is {}", v.unwrap_or_default()))
        .collect();
    Some(match ids.is_empty() {
        true => format!("\"{key}\""),
        false => format!("\"{key}\" where {}", ids.join(" and ")),
    })
}

/// A key that says what an entry is (rather than where or how much).
fn identity_key(k: &str) -> bool {
    let k = k.to_lowercase();
    !slot_key(&k) && ["id", "type", "kind", "name"].iter().any(|n| k.contains(n))
}

/// A key that says which inventory slot an entry is in. Only these names: a key that moves
/// (a sort position) would lose the value.
fn slot_key(k: &str) -> bool {
    ["index", "slot", "slot_index", "slotindex", "slot_id", "slotid"].contains(&k.to_lowercase().as_str())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn text_round_trip() {
        let p = DictPath::parse("{amount|id=0,data,index}").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(p.with, vec![("id".into(), Some(0)), ("data".into(), None), ("index".into(), None)]);
        assert_eq!(p.text(), "{amount|id=0,data,index}");
        assert_eq!(p.describe(), "\"amount\" where \"id\" is 0");
        assert_eq!(DictPath::parse("{amount|id=-3}").unwrap().with, vec![("id".into(), Some(-3))]);
        assert!(DictPath::parse("{amo unt|id}").is_none());
        assert!(DictPath::parse("\"Inventory\"@10,+38").is_none());
        let p = DictPath::parse("{amount|id=1,data,index=7}").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(p.describe(), "\"amount\" where \"id\" is 1 and \"index\" is 7");
        assert!(p.has_slot() && !p.any_slot().has_slot());
        assert_eq!(p.any_slot().text(), "{amount|id=1,data,index}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn slot_keys() {
        assert!(slot_key("index") && slot_key("Slot") && slot_key("slot_id"));
        assert!(!identity_key("slot_id") && identity_key("item_id") && !slot_key("position"));
    }
}
```

`helper/src/helper.rs`:

```rs
// The part that runs on the host (started by the frontend through
// `flatpak-spawn --host`). Reads and writes game memory through `Mem` (mem.rs); what it asks
// the OS about other programs goes through `os` (linux.rs).
// Protocol: one command per line on stdin; each reply ends with a line "end".

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fs::{self, File};
use std::io::{self, BufRead, Write};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use crate::anticheat;
use crate::ue::{self, UePath};
use crate::gdscript::{self, ScriptPath};
use crate::godot::{self, DictPath};
use crate::names::{self, Heap, NamedPath};
use crate::pointers::{self, Module, Pointers, PtrPath};
use crate::launchers;
use crate::mono::{self, MonoPath};
use crate::js::{self, JsPath};
use crate::gml::{self, GmlPath};
use crate::lua::{self, LuaPath};
use crate::air::{self, AirPath};
use crate::java::{self, JavaPath};
use crate::python::{self, PyPath};
use crate::trace;
use crate::mem::{FileAt, Mem};
use crate::os;

pub struct Region {
    pub start: u64,
    pub end: u64,
    pub perms: String,
    pub path: String,
}

pub use crate::os::maps;

/// A region mapped from a file: Linux paths start with '/', Windows ones with a drive ("C:/").
pub fn from_file(path: &str) -> bool {
    path.starts_with('/') || path.as_bytes().get(1..3) == Some(b":/")
}
use crate::os::environ;

/// The program as started (argv[0]); Wine paths have spaces ("E:\\Mass Effect Andromeda\\...").
fn argv0(pid: u32) -> String {
    os::argv(pid).into_iter().next().unwrap_or_default()
}

/// The program's arguments (without the program itself).
fn args(pid: u32) -> Vec<String> {
    os::argv(pid).into_iter().skip(1).filter(|a| !a.is_empty()).collect()
}

fn cmdline(pid: u32) -> String {
    os::argv(pid).into_iter().filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ")
}

/// File name of the program, also for Windows programs under Wine.
pub fn exe_name(pid: u32) -> String {
    argv0(pid).rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or_default().to_owned()
}

/// The name a game goes by (the games list, its profile): the program's, except for players
/// that run many games, named after the game file they were started with. Ruffle runs every
/// Flash game: all of them shared one name and one profile (Age of War's saved values were
/// restored into The Binding of Isaac); Solarus's `solarus-run` every Solarus quest. Started
/// without a file (opened from its menu), it keeps the player's name.
pub fn game_name(pid: u32) -> String {
    if let Some(name) = nwjs_app(pid).map(|dir| nwjs_name(pid, &dir)) {
        return name;
    }
    let exe = exe_name(pid);
    let lower = exe.to_ascii_lowercase();
    if DOSBOXES.contains(&lower.trim_end_matches(".exe")) {
        let home = std::env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_default();
        return dosbox_game(&argv0(pid), &os::cwd(pid), &home).map_or(exe, |g| format!("{g} (DOSBox)"));
    }
    let args: Vec<String> = os::argv(pid).into_iter().skip(1).collect();
    run_game(&lower, &args, || os::cwd(pid)).unwrap_or(exe)
}

/// The game a player program was started with (`game_name`): the game file it was given, a
/// LÖVE game's folder, a Python game's script (its folder when the script has a name every game
/// uses, like main.py). LÖVE, Java and Python run many games each with the same code: values
/// saved by code pattern in one would be found in another.
fn run_game(program: &str, args: &[String], cwd: impl Fn() -> String) -> Option<String> {
    let program = program.trim_end_matches(".exe");
    let endings: &[&str] = match program {
        "ruffle" => &[".swf"],
        "solarus-run" => &[".solarus"],
        "love" | "lovec" => &[".love"],
        "java" | "javaw" => return java_game(args),
        "mono" | "mono-sgen" => &[".exe"],
        p if is_python(p) => &[".py", ".pyc", ".pyw", ".pyz"],
        _ => return None,
    };
    // A path or a URL; a URL's query left out.
    let file = |a: &str| a.split(['?', '#']).next().unwrap_or_default().rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or_default().to_owned();
    let full = |a: &str| if a.starts_with('/') { a.to_owned() } else { format!("{}/{a}", cwd()) };
    if let Some(a) = args.iter().find(|a| endings.iter().any(|e| file(a).to_ascii_lowercase().ends_with(e))) {
        let name = file(a);
        let stem = name.rsplit_once('.').map_or(name.as_str(), |(s, _)| s).to_ascii_lowercase();
        if !is_python(program) || !["main", "__main__", "game", "run", "run_game", "start", "play", "launcher"].contains(&stem.as_str()) {
            return Some(name);
        }
        let path = full(a);
        let folder = path.split('/').rev().skip(1).find(|d| !d.is_empty() && *d != "." && !["src", "game", "bin", "data"].contains(d))?;
        return Some(format!("{folder} (Python)"));
    }
    // `python -m <module>`, `love <folder>` (a game kept as a folder; "." is the one it runs in).
    if is_python(program) {
        return args.iter().position(|a| a == "-m").and_then(|i| args.get(i + 1)).cloned();
    }
    if program.starts_with("love") {
        let path = full(args.iter().find(|a| !a.starts_with('-'))?);
        return path.split('/').rev().find(|d| !d.is_empty() && *d != ".").map(|d| format!("{d} (LÖVE)"));
    }
    None
}

/// The game Java runs: the jar of `-jar <file>`, else the main class (`-cp <jars> <class>`), or
/// the module of `-m <module>/<class>`.
fn java_game(args: &[String]) -> Option<String> {
    let mut args = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = args.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "-jar" => return args.next().map(|f| f.rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or_default().to_owned()),
            "-m" | "--module" => return args.next().cloned(),
            "-cp" | "-classpath" | "--class-path" | "-p" | "--module-path" | "--add-modules" | "--add-opens" | "--add-exports"
            | "--add-reads" | "--patch-module" | "--limit-modules" | "--upgrade-module-path" => {
                args.next();
            }
            a if !a.starts_with('-') => return Some(a.to_owned()),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    None
}

/// Python, as a program: python, python3, python3.12, python2.7, pythonw.exe.
fn is_python(program: &str) -> bool {
    let p = program.trim_end_matches(".exe").trim_end_matches('w');
    p.strip_prefix("python").is_some_and(|v| v.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '.'))
}

/// Python running a Wine launcher (Proton's `proton` script, GE-Proton's too, or `umu-run`)
/// rather than a game. Steam injects its overlay into every process of a launch and the overlay
/// needs libGL, so Proton's launcher loads the GPU driver and looks like a pygame game.
fn wine_launcher(args: &[String]) -> bool {
    let script = args.iter().find(|a| !a.starts_with('-'));
    script.is_some_and(|a| ["proton", "umu-run", "umu_run.py"].contains(&a.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or_default()))
}

/// DOSBox and its forks, as programs (".exe" left off).
const DOSBOXES: &[&str] = &["dosbox", "dosbox-x", "dosbox-staging"];

/// The DOS game a DOSBox runs, by its folder: every DOSBox game is `dosbox.exe`, and all of them
/// shared one profile (GOG and Steam ship DOS games each with its own DOSBox: Tyrian 2000's is
/// `Tyrian 2000\DOSBOX\dosbox.exe`). The program's folder, or the one above it when that is
/// DOSBox's own; for a DOSBox installed system-wide (Lutris, a flatpak), the folder it runs in.
fn dosbox_game(argv0: &str, cwd: &str, home: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let parts = |p: &str| -> Vec<String> { p.split(['/', '\\']).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).map(str::to_owned).collect() };
    let game = |mut dirs: Vec<String>| {
        // DOSBox's own folder, and GOG's Linux layout (<game>/dosbox, <game>/data).
        while dirs.last().is_some_and(|d| {
            let d = d.to_ascii_lowercase();
            d.contains("dosbox") || ["game", "data", "bin"].contains(&d.as_str())
        }) {
            dirs.pop();
        }
        // A drive letter alone ("S:") isn't a game.
        dirs.pop().filter(|d| !d.ends_with(':'))
    };
    // A relative path ("dosbox/dosbox", as GOG's Linux start.sh runs it) is from the folder it
    // runs in; a Windows one starts with a drive.
    let absolute = argv0.starts_with('/') || argv0.get(1..2) == Some(":");
    let mut exe_dirs = if absolute { parts(argv0) } else { parts(&format!("{cwd}/{argv0}")) };
    exe_dirs.pop();
    let system = ["usr", "app", "bin", "sbin", "snap"].contains(&exe_dirs.first().map_or("", String::as_str));
    if let Some(g) = (argv0.contains(['/', '\\']) && !system).then(|| game(exe_dirs)).flatten() {
        return Some(g);
    }
    let cwd = cwd.trim_end_matches('/');
    if cwd.is_empty() || cwd == home.trim_end_matches('/') {
        return None;
    }
    game(parts(cwd))
}

/// The folder of the NW.js app a process belongs to (RPG Maker MV, Construct and other HTML5
/// games): its program sits next to package.json or package.nw and NW.js's own files.
/// Native programs only (Wine's are told apart by their .exe, not looked at yet).
fn nwjs_app(pid: u32) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let program = os::exe(pid)?;
    let dir = program.parent()?;
    let inside = os::inside(pid, dir);
    let has = |f: &str| inside.join(f).exists();
    ((has("package.json") || has("package.nw")) && (has("nw.pak") || has("resources.pak") || has("lib/libnw.so"))).then(|| dir.to_path_buf())
}

/// An NW.js game runs its JavaScript, and keeps its values, in a Chromium renderer process
/// (`--type=renderer`; NW.js 0.12's renderers are forked from its zygote and keep the zygote's
/// command line); the window's own process (GTK) and the GPU process hold none of them.
fn nwjs_renderer(pid: u32) -> bool {
    let cmd = cmdline(pid);
    let parent = os::parent(pid);
    cmd.contains(" --type=renderer") || cmd.contains(" --type=zygote") && parent.is_some_and(|p| cmdline(p).contains(" --type=zygote"))
}

/// An NW.js game's name: an RPG Maker game's title (`www/data/System.json`), else its folder's.
fn nwjs_name(pid: u32, dir: &Path) -> String {
    let inside = os::inside(pid, dir);
    let title = fs::read_to_string(inside.join("www/data/System.json"))
        .ok()
        .and_then(|t| crate::json::parse(&t))
        .and_then(|v| v.get("gameTitle").and_then(|t| t.str()).map(|t| t.trim().replace('\t', " ")))
        .filter(|t| !t.is_empty());
    title.unwrap_or_else(|| dir.file_name().map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).unwrap_or_else(|| "NW.js game".into()))
}

/// GameMaker games keep every number as a double; they ship their assets as data.win (or
/// game.unx on Linux) next to the program.
fn is_gamemaker(pid: u32, exe: &str) -> bool {
    let Ok(regions) = maps(pid) else { return false };
    regions.iter().filter(|r| r.path.rsplit('/').next().is_some_and(|n| n.eq_ignore_ascii_case(exe))).any(|r| {
        let dir = std::path::Path::new(&r.path).with_file_name("");
        ["data.win", "game.unx", "assets/game.unx"].iter().any(|f| dir.join(f).exists())
    })
}

/// Java games run on a JVM (HotSpot's libjvm.so, or jvm.dll under Proton). Its garbage collector
/// moves objects around, and one instruction of its bytecode interpreter writes the int fields
/// of every object: a code pattern found there led a limit into another object's reference field
/// and crashed Shattered Pixel Dungeon.
fn is_java(pid: u32) -> bool {
    let Ok(regions) = maps(pid) else { return false };
    regions.iter().any(|r| {
        let name = r.path.rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or_default();
        name == "libjvm.so" || name.eq_ignore_ascii_case("jvm.dll")
    })
}

/// Memory scramblers: Unity games using CodeStage Anti-Cheat Toolkit's obscured types keep their
/// numbers XORed with a per-value key, next to a plain decoy the game rewrites (Moonlighter's
/// health). Found by its namespace in the game's assemblies (Mono) or IL2CPP's metadata, in
/// <Game>_Data (from the maps, else next to the program).
fn scrambler(pid: u32, regions: &[Region]) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let mapped = regions.iter().find_map(|r| r.path.find("_Data/").map(|i| PathBuf::from(&r.path[..i + 5])));
    let beside = || {
        let program = program_path(pid, regions)?;
        Some(program.with_file_name(format!("{}_Data", program.file_stem()?.to_string_lossy())))
    };
    let data = mapped.or_else(beside)?;
    let data = os::inside(pid, &data);
    let assembly = |p: &PathBuf| {
        let name = p.file_name().map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().to_ascii_lowercase()).unwrap_or_default();
        name.ends_with(".dll") && (name.starts_with("assembly-csharp") || name.starts_with("actk"))
    };
    let managed = fs::read_dir(data.join("Managed")).into_iter().flatten().flatten().map(|e| e.path()).filter(assembly);
    let metadata = data.join("il2cpp_data/Metadata/global-metadata.dat");
    let needle = b"CodeStage.AntiCheat.ObscuredTypes";
    let uses = |p: PathBuf| fs::read(p).is_ok_and(|b| b.windows(needle.len()).any(|w| w == needle));
    managed.chain([metadata]).any(uses).then_some("CodeStage Anti-Cheat Toolkit")
}

/// The program a process runs (`program_path`).
fn program_of(pid: u32) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    maps(pid).ok().and_then(|m| program_path(pid, &m))
}

/// Adobe AIR games (air.rs): the AIR runtime mapped.
fn is_air(pid: u32) -> bool {
    maps(pid).is_ok_and(|r| air::runs_air(&r))
}

/// Python games (python.rs): CPython mapped (libpython, Ren'Py's librenpython) or running.
fn is_python_game(pid: u32, exe: &str) -> bool {
    maps(pid).is_ok_and(|r| python::runs_python(&r, exe))
}

/// Lua games (lua.rs): a Lua library mapped (LÖVE's LuaJIT), or Defold's engine.
fn is_lua(pid: u32) -> bool {
    let Ok(regions) = maps(pid) else { return false };
    lua::runs_lua(pid, &regions, program_path(pid, &regions).as_deref())
}

/// RPG Maker MV games (js.rs): NW.js running `www/js/rpg_core.js` from next to the program.
fn is_rpgmaker(pid: u32) -> bool {
    let program = maps(pid).ok().and_then(|m| program_path(pid, &m));
    js::is_rpgmaker(pid, program.as_deref())
}

/// Godot games load <program>.pck from next to the program, or carry it at the end of the
/// program (which then ends with its magic, "GDPC").
fn is_godot(pid: u32) -> bool {
    let Some(program) = maps(pid).ok().and_then(|m| program_path(pid, &m)) else { return false };
    let inside = |p: &Path| os::inside(pid, p);
    if inside(&program.with_extension("pck")).exists() || program.with_extension("pck").exists() {
        return true;
    }
    let ends_with_magic = |p: &Path| {
        let Ok(f) = File::open(p) else { return false };
        let Ok(len) = f.metadata().map(|m| m.len()) else { return false };
        let mut b = [0u8; 4];
        len >= 4 && f.read_exact_at(&mut b, len - 4).is_ok() && &b == b"GDPC"
    };
    ends_with_magic(&inside(&program)) || ends_with_magic(&program)
}

/// Why Ferret won't touch a game: the line is no cheating where other players or the player's
/// account can be reached.
enum Refusal {
    /// Loaded in the game, or running beside it in its Wine prefix.
    AntiCheat(String),
    /// Running elsewhere on the computer (Windows: anti-cheat runs as services and kernel
    /// drivers that see every program, not only its game's).
    #[cfg_attr(not(windows), allow(dead_code))]
    AntiCheatElsewhere(String),
    /// Its store lists it as played only with others (or as an MMO or a battle royale).
    Online,
    /// Steam lists Valve Anti-Cheat; it can't be seen running (it's in the Steam client).
    Vac,
    /// Its characters get flagged online for edits made offline (`launchers::FLAGS_EDITS`).
    FlagsEdits,
}

impl Refusal {
    /// The games list's word for it.
    fn code(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Refusal::AntiCheat(ac) => format!("anti-cheat {ac}"),
            Refusal::AntiCheatElsewhere(ac) => format!("anti-cheat-elsewhere {ac}"),
            Refusal::Online => "online".into(),
            Refusal::Vac => "vac".into(),
            Refusal::FlagsEdits => "edits".into(),
        }
    }

    fn why(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Refusal::AntiCheat(ac) => format!("{ac} is running with the game"),
            Refusal::AntiCheatElsewhere(ac) => format!("{ac} is running on the computer"),
            Refusal::Online => "the game is played online only".into(),
            Refusal::Vac => "the game uses Valve Anti-Cheat (Source games started with -insecure are allowed)".into(),
            Refusal::FlagsEdits => "the game flags edited characters when they go online".into(),
        }
    }
}

struct Verdict {
    refused: Option<Refusal>,
    /// Anti-cheat shipped in its folder or listed for it but not running: only a warning
    /// (most such games have a single-player mode that runs without it).
    ships: Option<String>,
}

/// Anti-cheat running now outside the games: `programs` (running in a Wine prefix: the prefix
/// and its name; on Windows anywhere on the computer, prefix empty) and `resident`, anti-cheat
/// that is always on (Windows: `anticheat::RESIDENT`), a warning only.
#[derive(Default)]
struct OnComputer {
    programs: Vec<(String, &'static str)>,
    resident: Option<&'static str>,
}

/// Blocked: anti-cheat running, online only, VAC (unless it can't reach secured servers), or a
/// game that flags edited characters. Warned: anti-cheat shipped or listed but not running.
/// `running` = `on_computer()`.
fn verdict(pid: u32, running: &OnComputer) -> Verdict {
    let maps = maps(pid).unwrap_or_default();
    let env = environ(pid);
    let about = about(&env);
    let refused = if let Some(r) = running_anti_cheat(&maps, &env, &running.programs) {
        Some(r)
    } else if about.online_only {
        Some(Refusal::Online)
    } else if about.flags_edits {
        Some(Refusal::FlagsEdits)
    } else if about.vac && !vac_safe(pid, &maps) {
        Some(Refusal::Vac)
    } else {
        None
    };
    let ships = if refused.is_some() { None } else { shipped_anti_cheat(pid, &maps, &env, about.listed) };
    Verdict { refused, ships }
}

/// The Wine prefix a program runs in (Proton's, Heroic's, Lutris's, umu's).
#[cfg(not(windows))]
fn wine_prefix(env: &HashMap<String, String>) -> Option<&String> {
    env.get("WINEPREFIX").or_else(|| env.get("STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH")).filter(|p| !p.is_empty())
}

/// Anti-cheat running now outside games. Linux: anti-cheat programs and the Wine prefix each
/// runs in (under Proton EasyAntiCheat_EOS.exe, BEService.exe and start_protected_game.exe run
/// beside the game). Windows: anti-cheat programs, services and drivers anywhere on the
/// computer (they watch every program there), and resident ones apart.
fn on_computer() -> OnComputer {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        let names = os::running_programs();
        let mut programs: Vec<(String, &'static str)> = Vec::new();
        for ac in names.iter().filter(|n| !anticheat::resident(n)).filter_map(|n| anticheat::named(n)) {
            if !programs.iter().any(|(_, a)| *a == ac) {
                programs.push((String::new(), ac));
            }
        }
        let resident = names.iter().filter(|n| anticheat::resident(n)).find_map(|n| anticheat::named(n));
        OnComputer { programs, resident }
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    OnComputer {
        programs: os::own_pids()
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|pid| {
                let ac = anticheat::named(&exe_name(pid))?;
                Some((wine_prefix(&environ(pid))?.clone(), ac))
            })
            .collect(),
        resident: None,
    }
}

/// Anti-cheat loaded in the game, running in its Wine prefix, or (Windows) on the computer.
fn running_anti_cheat(maps: &[Region], env: &HashMap<String, String>, programs: &[(String, &'static str)]) -> Option<Refusal> {
    if let Some(ac) = maps.iter().find_map(|r| anticheat::in_path(&r.path)) {
        return Some(Refusal::AntiCheat(ac.to_owned()));
    }
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        let _ = env;
        programs.first().map(|(_, ac)| Refusal::AntiCheatElsewhere((*ac).to_owned()))
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        let prefix = wine_prefix(env)?;
        programs.iter().find(|(p, _)| p == prefix).map(|(_, ac)| Refusal::AntiCheat((*ac).to_owned()))
    }
}

/// Anti-cheat that started in the attached game (or, on Windows, on the computer) since the
/// last look.
fn started_anti_cheat(pid: u32) -> Option<Refusal> {
    let maps = maps(pid).ok()?;
    running_anti_cheat(&maps, &environ(pid), &on_computer().programs)
}

/// Call of Duty's single-player programs, shipped beside the multiplayer ones of the same Steam
/// app (which Steam lists with VAC). Not checked on the games yet.
const SINGLE_PLAYER_PROGRAMS: &[&str] = &["iw3sp.exe", "iw4sp.exe", "iw5sp.exe", "t6sp.exe"];

/// A VAC game that can't reach VAC-secured servers: a single-player program, or a Source or
/// GoldSrc game started with -insecure (Valve: it can't join secured servers then). Only for
/// those engines: other games ignore the option.
fn vac_safe(pid: u32, maps: &[Region]) -> bool {
    if SINGLE_PLAYER_PROGRAMS.contains(&exe_name(pid).to_ascii_lowercase().as_str()) {
        return true;
    }
    let insecure = os::argv(pid).iter().any(|a| a.eq_ignore_ascii_case("-insecure"));
    let engine = |r: &Region| {
        let name = r.path.rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or_default().to_ascii_lowercase();
        ["tier0.dll", "libtier0.so", "libtier0_client.so", "hw.dll", "hw.so", "sw.dll"].contains(&name.as_str())
    };
    insecure && maps.iter().any(engine)
}

/// Anti-cheat shipped in the game's folder, or listed by AreWeAntiCheatYet for it (`listed`:
/// what its launcher's IDs found there).
fn shipped_anti_cheat(pid: u32, maps: &[Region], env: &HashMap<String, String>, listed: Option<String>) -> Option<String> {
    if listed.is_some() {
        return listed;
    }
    // Seen from inside the game's sandbox (pressure-vessel, flatpak).
    let inside = |p: &Path| os::inside(pid, p);
    let folder = match env.get("STEAM_COMPAT_INSTALL_PATH") {
        Some(dir) => PathBuf::from(dir),
        None => anticheat::game_folder(&program_path(pid, maps)?),
    };
    if let Some(ac) = anticheat::in_folder(&inside(&folder)) {
        return Some(ac.to_owned());
    }
    // Any launcher (or none): the folders and program named like a listed game.
    let exe = exe_name(pid);
    // Unreal: <game>/<project>/Binaries/Win64, so two folders up as well.
    let folders = folder.ancestors().take(3).filter_map(Path::file_name);
    let names: Vec<String> =
        folders.chain(Path::new(&exe).file_stem()).map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).collect();
    launchers::listed_as(&env, &names)
}

/// The program's file, as the game's sandbox sees it: Wine maps the .exe by its Linux path,
/// native programs are their own (`os::exe`).
fn program_path(pid: u32, maps: &[Region]) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let exe = exe_name(pid);
    let mapped = maps.iter().map(|r| Path::new(&r.path)).find(|p| p.file_name().is_some_and(|n| n.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&*exe)));
    match mapped {
        Some(p) => Some(p.to_path_buf()),
        None => os::exe(pid),
    }
}

/// Unreal games start as <game>/<Project>.exe, a stub that only starts
/// <game>/<Project>/Binaries/Win64/<Project>-Win64-Shipping.exe and waits for it: the stub's
/// folder when `program` is such a game.
fn unreal_stub_folder(program: &Path) -> Option<&Path> {
    let binaries = program.parent()?.parent()?;
    if !binaries.file_name()?.eq_ignore_ascii_case("binaries") {
        return None;
    }
    binaries.parent()?.parent()
}

/// The Steam app ID a game was started with (umu sets 0 or "default" for games not on Steam).
fn steam_id(env: &HashMap<String, String>) -> Option<&String> {
    ["SteamAppId", "SteamGameId"]
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|k| env.get(*k))
        .find(|id| *id != "0" && !id.is_empty() && id.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()))
}

fn about(env: &HashMap<String, String>) -> launchers::About {
    launchers::about(env, steam_id(env).and_then(|id| id.parse().ok()))
}

// --- How a value is stored. Addresses in commands are "<hex>[:type]", i32 when left out.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub(crate) enum Kind {
    I32,
    F32,
    F64,
    /// A 4-byte integer hidden from cheat tools: the word at the address XOR the next word
    /// (the key). The game re-encodes it with the same key on every change.
    Xor,
    /// A 2-byte whole number, unsigned: Frostbite keeps ammo so (Andromeda: loaded and reserve
    /// side by side, read with movzx); read as 4 bytes, the two together never match.
    U16,
    /// A GameMaker value (gml.rs): 16 bytes {value, flags, kind}, read as the kind of number it
    /// holds now (a double, an int32 or an int64: the game turns one into another as it likes),
    /// written as a double. Never searched for: values saved by a GameMaker path get it.
    Gm,
    /// A Lua value (lua.rs): 8 bytes, a double while it holds a number; never written once it
    /// holds something else (a table that grew moved its entries: the old place is freed).
    /// Values saved by a Lua path get it.
    Lua,
    /// A Python value (python.rs): the slot pointing to a number object (Python's numbers are
    /// immutable objects), read as the number it points to, written in place or by pointing
    /// the slot to a cached small int (`python::write_slot`). Values saved by a Python path.
    Py,
}

impl Kind {
    /// The kinds searches look for (all but `Gm` and `Lua`).
    const ALL: [Kind; 5] = [Kind::I32, Kind::F32, Kind::F64, Kind::Xor, Kind::U16];

    fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Kind::I32 => "i32",
            Kind::F32 => "f32",
            Kind::F64 => "f64",
            Kind::Xor => "xor",
            Kind::U16 => "u16",
            Kind::Gm => "gm",
            Kind::Lua => "lua",
            Kind::Py => "py",
        }
    }

    fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Kind> {
        Kind::ALL.into_iter().chain([Kind::Gm, Kind::Lua, Kind::Py]).find(|k| k.name() == s)
    }

    fn size(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Kind::U16 => 2,
            Kind::I32 | Kind::F32 => 4,
            Kind::F64 | Kind::Xor | Kind::Lua | Kind::Py => 8,
            Kind::Gm => 16,
        }
    }

    fn decode(self, b: &[u8]) -> f64 {
        match self {
            Kind::I32 => i32::from_le_bytes(b[..4].try_into().unwrap()) as f64,
            Kind::F32 => f32::from_le_bytes(b[..4].try_into().unwrap()) as f64,
            Kind::F64 => f64::from_le_bytes(b[..8].try_into().unwrap()),
            Kind::U16 => u16::from_le_bytes(b[..2].try_into().unwrap()) as f64,
            Kind::Xor => {
                (i32::from_le_bytes(b[..4].try_into().unwrap()) ^ i32::from_le_bytes(b[4..8].try_into().unwrap())) as f64
            }
            Kind::Gm => gml::rvalue_number(b).unwrap_or(f64::NAN),
            Kind::Lua => lua::number(b).unwrap_or(f64::NAN),
            // Read through the slot (`read_value`).
            Kind::Py => f64::NAN,
        }
    }

    /// Whether a value that went from `lo` to `hi` (either way round) meanwhile can be what the
    /// screen showed as `n`. Games show fractions rounded, cut off or rounded up (countdowns:
    /// Lumencraft's wave timer shows 6:37 with 396.4 s left); a decimal like 1.2 may be kept as
    /// a whole number of tenths (12).
    fn fits(self, lo: f64, hi: f64, n: Shown) -> bool {
        let (lo, hi) = (lo.min(hi), lo.max(hi));
        match self {
            Kind::I32 | Kind::Xor | Kind::U16 => lo <= n.scaled && n.scaled <= hi,
            Kind::F32 | Kind::F64 | Kind::Gm | Kind::Lua | Kind::Py => lo < n.value + n.step && hi > n.value - n.step,
        }
    }

    fn show(self, v: f64) -> String {
        match self {
            Kind::F32 => (v as f32).to_string(),
            _ => v.to_string(),
        }
    }
}

/// A number read off the screen: "1250", "1.2", "-3".
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Shown {
    value: f64,
    /// The last shown digit's worth: 1, 0.1, 0.01...
    step: f64,
    /// All digits as one whole number: 1.2 -> 12.
    scaled: f64,
}

impl Shown {
    fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Shown> {
        let value: f64 = s.parse().ok().filter(|v: &f64| v.is_finite())?;
        if !s.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || c == b'.' || c == b'-') {
            return None;
        }
        let decimals = s.split_once('.').map_or(0, |(_, b)| b.len() as i32);
        let scaled = s.replace('.', "").parse::<f64>().ok()?;
        Some(Shown { value, step: 10f64.powi(-decimals), scaled })
    }
}

fn read_value(mem: &Mem, addr: u64, kind: Kind) -> Option<f64> {
    if kind == Kind::Py {
        return python::read_slot(mem, addr);
    }
    let mut b = [0u8; 16];
    mem.read_exact_at(&mut b[..kind.size()], addr).ok()?;
    Some(kind.decode(&b)).filter(|v| !matches!(kind, Kind::Gm | Kind::Lua) || !v.is_nan())
}

fn write_value(mem: &Mem, addr: u64, kind: Kind, v: f64) -> io::Result<()> {
    match kind {
        Kind::I32 => mem.write_all_at(&(v.round() as i32).to_le_bytes(), addr),
        Kind::F32 => mem.write_all_at(&(v as f32).to_le_bytes(), addr),
        Kind::F64 => mem.write_all_at(&v.to_le_bytes(), addr),
        Kind::U16 => mem.write_all_at(&(v.round().clamp(0.0, 65535.0) as u16).to_le_bytes(), addr),
        Kind::Xor => {
            let mut key = [0u8; 4];
            mem.read_exact_at(&mut key, addr + 4)?;
            mem.write_all_at(&((v.round() as i32) ^ i32::from_le_bytes(key)).to_le_bytes(), addr)
        }
        // A number of any kind becomes a double (kind 0); the flags stay.
        Kind::Gm => {
            let mut b = [0u8; 16];
            mem.read_exact_at(&mut b, addr)?;
            if gml::rvalue_number(&b).is_none() {
                return Err(io::Error::other("not a GameMaker number now"));
            }
            mem.write_all_at(&v.to_le_bytes(), addr)?;
            mem.write_all_at(&0u32.to_le_bytes(), addr + 12)
        }
        Kind::Lua => {
            let mut b = [0u8; 8];
            mem.read_exact_at(&mut b, addr)?;
            if lua::number(&b).is_none() {
                return Err(io::Error::other("not a Lua number now"));
            }
            mem.write_all_at(&v.to_le_bytes(), addr)
        }
        Kind::Py => python::write_slot(mem, addr, v),
    }
}

/// "<hex>[:type]"
fn parse_loc(a: &str) -> Option<(u64, Kind)> {
    let (addr, kind) = match a.split_once(':') {
        Some((addr, kind)) => (addr, Kind::parse(kind)?),
        None => (a, Kind::I32),
    };
    Some((parse_addr(addr)?, kind))
}

/// Writable memory that can hold the game's values. Not the GPU driver's mappings
/// (`/dev/nvidia0`, `/dev/dri/*`, dma-bufs): video memory reads very slowly through
/// `/proc/<pid>/mem` (on Creeper World 4, 157 MB of them took 3.7 s of a 4 s pass; the game's
/// own 1.2 GB took 0.3 s).
pub fn scannable(r: &Region) -> bool {
    let device = r.path.starts_with("/dev/") && !r.path.starts_with("/dev/shm/") && !r.path.starts_with("/dev/zero");
    r.perms.starts_with("rw")
        && !device
        && !r.path.contains("dmabuf")
        && !matches!(r.path.as_str(), "[vvar]" | "[vvar_vclock]" | "[vsyscall]")
}

// --- Limits: keep a value within a range, writing only when the game moves it out.

struct Limit {
    name: String,
    addr: u64,
    kind: Kind,
    min: Option<f64>,
    max: Option<f64>,
    sites: Vec<Site>,
    /// Pointer paths to the value; when there are any, the value is found through them on
    /// every check instead of through `sites` and the guard.
    paths: Vec<PtrPath>,
    /// A named path to every place the value is kept (all of an item's stacks): when there is
    /// one, all of them are found through it on every check and kept in range.
    named: Option<NamedLimit>,
    // First bytes of the object holding the value (its type pointer). If they
    // change, the object is gone and writing would corrupt unrelated memory. 0: no object (see
    // `guard_of`).
    guard_addr: u64,
    guard: [u8; 4],
    fixes: u64,
    restores: u64,
    /// Found through pointer paths: whether the game has changed the value at the place they
    /// lead to since they first led there, and the value seen there until it does. Before the
    /// value exists (a game's menu) paths may agree on another place (Age of War's title menu:
    /// 154 of 247 on a place holding 0); the game changing it shows it's the value.
    changed: bool,
    unchanged: Option<f64>,
    paused: Option<&'static str>,
    /// Turned off by the player (`switch`, a hotkey): still followed, never written.
    off: bool,
    retry_at: Instant,
    /// When its code patterns last found it (the object may be replaced while the old one stays
    /// readable, which the guard can't see).
    checked_at: Instant,
    /// Whether all its code patterns were searched for a static pointer to the object.
    searched_code: bool,
    /// A thread is finding it by its code patterns now (`limiter_loop`): not started again.
    finding: bool,
    /// How long until its code patterns are checked again: `RECHECK_EVERY`, doubled every time
    /// they find it where it was, up to `RECHECK_MOST` (the check stops every game thread for
    /// a moment); back to `RECHECK_EVERY` once it moved.
    recheck_every: Duration,
}

/// A named path of any kind: through objects the game names (Unity, names.rs), to an entry of
/// the game's dictionaries (Godot, godot.rs), through its scripts' variables (Godot,
/// gdscript.rs), through its Unreal objects (ue.rs), to a field of a Mono class's live
/// objects (Unity, Mono or IL2CPP; mono.rs), from an RPG Maker MV game's globals (js.rs) or
/// to a GameMaker instance's or the global object's variable (gml.rs).
#[derive(Clone)]
enum Named {
    Objects(NamedPath),
    Dict(DictPath),
    Script(ScriptPath),
    Unreal(UePath),
    Mono(MonoPath),
    Js(JsPath),
    Gml(GmlPath),
    Lua(LuaPath),
    Java(JavaPath),
    Py(PyPath),
    Air(AirPath),
}

impl Named {
    fn parse(text: &str) -> Option<Named> {
        if text.starts_with("ue:") {
            return UePath::parse(text).map(Named::Unreal);
        }
        if text.starts_with("gd:") {
            return ScriptPath::parse(text).map(Named::Script);
        }
        if text.starts_with("mono:") || text.starts_with("il2cpp:") {
            return MonoPath::parse(text).map(Named::Mono);
        }
        if text.starts_with("js:") {
            return JsPath::parse(text).map(Named::Js);
        }
        if text.starts_with("gml:") {
            return GmlPath::parse(text).map(Named::Gml);
        }
        if text.starts_with("lua:") {
            return LuaPath::parse(text).map(Named::Lua);
        }
        if text.starts_with("java:") {
            return JavaPath::parse(text).map(Named::Java);
        }
        if text.starts_with("py:") {
            return PyPath::parse(text).map(Named::Py);
        }
        if text.starts_with("air:") {
            return AirPath::parse(text).map(Named::Air);
        }
        match text.starts_with('{') {
            true => DictPath::parse(text).map(Named::Dict),
            false => NamedPath::parse(text).map(Named::Objects),
        }
    }

    fn is_named(text: &str) -> bool {
        text.starts_with('"') || text.starts_with('{') || text.starts_with("ue:") || text.starts_with("gd:") || text.starts_with("mono:") || text.starts_with("il2cpp:") || text.starts_with("js:") || text.starts_with("gml:") || text.starts_with("lua:") || text.starts_with("java:") || text.starts_with("py:") || text.starts_with("air:")
    }

    /// Walked again right before every write (not only every `LIMIT_FIND_EVERY`): Java moves
    /// its objects, and the old copy's memory is reused; Python makes a new number object at
    /// every change (`hp -= 1`) and frees the old one.
    fn fresh(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Named::Java(_) | Named::Py(_))
    }

    /// Where it leads from the roots found before (no search).
    fn walk(&self, heap: &Heap, roots: &[u64]) -> Vec<u64> {
        match self {
            Named::Objects(p) => heap.walk(roots, p),
            Named::Dict(p) => godot::walk(heap, roots, p),
            Named::Script(p) => gdscript::walk(heap, roots, p),
            Named::Mono(p) => mono::walk(heap, roots, p),
            Named::Js(p) => js::walk(heap, roots, p),
            Named::Gml(p) => gml::walk(heap, program_of(heap.pid).as_deref(), roots, p),
            Named::Lua(p) => lua::walk(heap, roots, p),
            Named::Java(p) => java::walk(heap, roots, p),
            Named::Py(p) => python::walk(heap, roots, p),
            Named::Air(p) => air::walk(heap, roots, p),
            Named::Unreal(p) => unreal(heap.pid, heap.mem()).map(|ue| ue.walk(heap.mem(), roots, p)).unwrap_or_default(),
        }
    }

    /// Searches the game's memory for its roots (seconds; Unreal's object list: a fraction of one).
    fn find_roots(&self, heap: &Heap) -> Vec<u64> {
        match self {
```
