```rs
//! Python games (CPython 2.7 and 3.x: Ren'Py visual novels, pygame games): their objects read
//! from outside. A value is named by the namespace it lives in and the names from there:
//! `py:store#souls` (a Ren'Py game's variable), `py:__main__#player.hp` (a pygame game's
//! global `player`, its attribute `hp`), `py:__main__#party[0].hp` (a list's element).
//!
//! Found by shape, no symbols: the `type` type is its own type and is named "type"; the builtin
//! types (dict, str, int, float, module...) are objects of type `type` with those names;
//! modules are objects of type `module`, each holding its namespace dict (Ren'Py's `store` is a
//! `StoreDict` of its own, found the same way). Layouts by version (CPython's headers 2.7,
//! 3.6-3.14): dicts (2.7 open tables; 3.6-3.10 and 3.11+ compact tables of keys with indices),
//! strings (3.3+ compact: characters after a 40-byte header in 3.12+, 48 before; 2.7: at +36),
//! ints (2.7: a C long at +16; 3.x: 30-bit digits at +24, the size or 3.12's tag at +16), an
//! object's attributes (its dict at `tp_dictoffset`; 3.11+ classes keep a dict or values before
//! or after the object, named by the class's shared keys).
//!
//! Python's numbers are immutable objects: a variable points to one, and `hp -= 1` makes a new
//! one. So a value's place is the slot pointing to its object (the `py` value type), and a write
//! changes the object in place only when nothing else points to it (`ob_refcnt` 1); small ints
//! (-5..256) are shared by the whole game, so the slot is pointed to the cached one instead
//! (3.12+: those are immortal; earlier, their count is raised by one).

use crate::mono::player_like;
use crate::names::Heap;
use crate::ue::{Listed, ListedObject, MAX_LISTED};
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet, VecDeque};
use crate::mem::Mem;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

/// Objects looked into for one list at most.
const MAX_VISITED: usize = 20000;
/// How deep the list goes from a namespace.
const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 10;
/// Entries read from one dict, list or tuple at most.
const MAX_ENTRIES: u64 = 1 << 16;
/// Elements listed from one list or tuple at most.
const MAX_ELEMENTS: u64 = 256;

// tp_flags bits.
const HEAPTYPE: u64 = 1 << 9;
const INLINE_VALUES: u64 = 1 << 2;
const MANAGED_DICT: u64 = 1 << 4;
const LIST_SUBCLASS: u64 = 1 << 25;
const TUPLE_SUBCLASS: u64 = 1 << 26;
const DICT_SUBCLASS: u64 = 1 << 29;
// PyTypeObject fields (the same from 2.7 to 3.14 on 64-bit).
const TP_NAME: u64 = 24;
const TP_BASICSIZE: u64 = 32;
const TP_FLAGS: u64 = 168;
const TP_DICTOFFSET: u64 = 288;

fn word(mem: &Mem, at: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    let mut b = [0u8; 8];
    mem.read_exact_at(&mut b, at).ok().map(|_| u64::from_le_bytes(b))
}

fn half(mem: &Mem, at: u64) -> Option<u32> {
    let mut b = [0u8; 4];
    mem.read_exact_at(&mut b, at).ok().map(|_| u32::from_le_bytes(b))
}

fn byte(mem: &Mem, at: u64) -> Option<u8> {
    let mut b = [0u8; 1];
    mem.read_exact_at(&mut b, at).ok().map(|_| b[0])
}

fn cstr(mem: &Mem, at: u64) -> Option<String> {
    if at < 0x10000 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut b = [0u8; 64];
    let n = mem.read_at(&mut b, at).ok()?;
    let end = b[..n].iter().position(|&c| c == 0)?;
    std::str::from_utf8(&b[..end]).ok().map(str::to_owned)
}

/// The version the game's Python reports in its libraries' names (libpython3.12.so,
/// python3.14, libpython2.7.so) or in Ren'Py 8's librenpython.so (its version string).
fn version(pid: u32, regions: &[crate::helper::Region]) -> Option<(u8, u8)> {
    let from_name = |n: &str| {
        let i = n.find("python")? + 6;
        let rest = &n[i..];
        let (maj, rest) = rest.split_once('.')?;
        let min: String = rest.chars().take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()).collect();
        Some((maj.parse().ok()?, min.parse().ok()?))
    };
    let names: Vec<&str> = regions.iter().map(|r| r.path.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or_default()).collect();
    if let Some(v) = names.iter().find_map(|n| from_name(n).filter(|&(maj, _): &(u8, u8)| maj == 2 || maj == 3)) {
        return Some(v);
    }
    let lib = regions.iter().find(|r| r.path.ends_with("/librenpython.so") || r.path.contains("/librenpython"))?;
    let data = std::fs::read(crate::os::inside(pid, std::path::Path::new(&lib.path))).ok()?;
    // Its paths and module names say "python3.12" (its first "3.x.y" string isn't always the
    // version: Ren'Py 8's had "3.3.x" earlier): the most common minor version wins.
    let mut counts: HashMap<u8, usize> = HashMap::new();
    for i in memchr_all(&data, b"python3.") {
        let minor: String = data[i + 8..].iter().take(2).take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()).map(|&c| c as char).collect();
        if let Ok(m) = minor.parse::<u8>() {
            *counts.entry(m).or_default() += 1;
        }
    }
    counts.into_iter().max_by_key(|&(_, n)| n).map(|(m, _)| (3, m))
}

/// Where a byte string occurs in a buffer.
fn memchr_all(data: &[u8], needle: &[u8]) -> Vec<usize> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    while let Some(p) = data[i..].iter().position(|&c| c == needle[0]) {
        let at = i + p;
        if data[at..].starts_with(needle) {
            out.push(at);
        }
        i = at + 1;
    }
    out
}

/// Whether the game runs CPython: a libpython or Ren'Py's librenpython mapped, or a python
/// program.
pub fn runs_python(regions: &[crate::helper::Region], exe: &str) -> bool {
    let python = |n: &str| n.strip_prefix("python").is_some_and(|v| v.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '.'));
    python(&exe.to_ascii_lowercase())
        || regions.iter().any(|r| {
            let n = r.path.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or_default();
            n.starts_with("libpython2") || n.starts_with("libpython3") || n.starts_with("librenpython") || python(n)
        })
}

/// A dict key: a name or a whole number.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
enum Key {
    Name(String),
    Index(i64),
}

/// The builtin types this game's Python has.
#[derive(Default, Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct Types {
    module: u64,
    dict: u64,
    str_: u64,
    int: u64,
    long: u64,
    float: u64,
    bool_: u64,
    list: u64,
    tuple: u64,
    store: u64,
}

/// A located game: its Python's version and types, and its namespaces by name.
pub struct Py {
    pid: u32,
    ver: (u8, u8),
    t: Types,
    /// Where a compact ASCII string's characters start (40 in 3.12+, 48 in 3.3-3.11).
    str_at: u64,
    roots: Mutex<(HashMap<String, u64>, Instant)>,
    /// Where a heap type keeps `ht_name` (then `ht_slots`, `ht_qualname`, `ht_cached_keys`).
    ht_name_at: Mutex<Option<u64>>,
    /// The cached small ints: the object for 0 (they're consecutive) and its size.
    small: Mutex<Option<(u64, u64)>>,
}

/// What a slot holds.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Debug)]
enum Val {
    Int(i64),
    Float(f64),
    /// A dict (or subclass), list, tuple or an object with attributes.
    Obj(u64),
    Other,
}

impl Py {
    fn locate(heap: &Heap) -> Option<Py> {
        if heap.width() != 8 {
            return None;
        }
        let mem = heap.mem();
        let regions = crate::helper::maps(heap.pid).ok()?;
        let ver = version(heap.pid, &regions)?;
        // The `type` type: its own type, named "type".
        let mut ty = 0;
        heap.each_chunk(0, |addr, b, fresh| {
            if ty != 0 {
                return;
            }
            for off in (0..fresh.saturating_sub(16)).step_by(8) {
                let w = u64::from_le_bytes(b[off + 8..off + 16].try_into().unwrap());
                if w == addr + off as u64 && word(mem, w + TP_NAME).and_then(|n| cstr(mem, n)).as_deref() == Some("type") {
                    ty = w;
                    return;
                }
            }
        });
        if ty == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        // The builtin types: objects of type `type` by name, not made by Python code (heap types).
        let mut t = Types::default();
        for r in heap.referrers(&[ty]) {
            let o = r - 8;
            let Some(name) = word(mem, o + TP_NAME).and_then(|n| cstr(mem, n)) else { continue };
            let heap_type = word(mem, o + TP_FLAGS).is_some_and(|f| f & HEAPTYPE != 0);
            let slot = match name.as_str() {
                "module" => &mut t.module,
                "dict" => &mut t.dict,
                "str" => &mut t.str_,
                "int" => &mut t.int,
                "long" => &mut t.long,
                "float" => &mut t.float,
                "bool" => &mut t.bool_,
                "list" => &mut t.list,
                "tuple" => &mut t.tuple,
                "StoreDict" => &mut t.store,
                _ => continue,
            };
            if *slot == 0 && (!heap_type || name == "StoreDict") {
                *slot = o;
            }
        }
        if t.module == 0 || t.dict == 0 || t.str_ == 0 || t.int == 0 || t.float == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let mut py = Py {
            pid: heap.pid,
            ver,
            t,
            str_at: if ver >= (3, 12) { 40 } else { 48 },
            roots: Mutex::new((HashMap::new(), Instant::now())),
            ht_name_at: Mutex::new(None),
            small: Mutex::new(None),
        };
        py.find_roots(heap);
        // The string layout, checked on the names found (a build could differ).
        if py.roots.lock().unwrap().0.is_empty() && ver.0 == 3 {
            py.str_at = if py.str_at == 40 { 48 } else { 40 };
            py.find_roots(heap);
        }
        Some(py)
    }

    /// The namespaces: every module's dict and Ren'Py's store dicts, by their `__name__`.
    fn find_roots(&self, heap: &Heap) {
        let mem = heap.mem();
        let targets: Vec<u64> = [self.t.module, self.t.store].into_iter().filter(|&x| x != 0).collect();
        let mut roots = HashMap::new();
        for r in heap.referrers(&targets) {
            let o = r - 8;
            let Some(ty) = word(mem, r) else { continue };
            let d = if ty == self.t.module { word(mem, o + 16).unwrap_or(0) } else { o };
            if d == 0 || !self.is_dict(mem, d) {
                continue;
            }
            let name = self.dict_get(mem, d, &Key::Name("__name__".into())).and_then(|(v, _)| self.text(mem, v));
            if let Some(name) = name {
                roots.entry(name).or_insert(d);
            }
        }
        *self.roots.lock().unwrap() = (roots, Instant::now());
    }

    fn type_of(&self, mem: &Mem, o: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        word(mem, o + 8).filter(|&t| t > 0x10000)
    }

    fn flags(&self, mem: &Mem, t: u64) -> u64 {
        word(mem, t + TP_FLAGS).unwrap_or(0)
    }

    fn is_dict(&self, mem: &Mem, o: u64) -> bool {
        self.type_of(mem, o).is_some_and(|t| t == self.t.dict || t == self.t.store || self.flags(mem, t) & DICT_SUBCLASS != 0)
    }

    /// A str's text (3.x compact strings; 2.7's byte strings).
    fn text(&self, mem: &Mem, o: u64) -> Option<String> {
        if self.type_of(mem, o)? != self.t.str_ {
            return None;
        }
        let len = word(mem, o + 16)?;
        if len > 256 {
            return None;
        }
        let (at, width) = if self.ver.0 == 2 {
            (36, 1)
        } else {
            let state = half(mem, o + 32)?;
            let (kind, compact, ascii) = ((state >> 2) & 7, state >> 5 & 1 == 1, state >> 6 & 1 == 1);
            if !compact {
                return None;
            }
            // Non-ASCII compact strings keep two more fields (utf8 length and pointer).
            (if ascii { self.str_at } else { self.str_at + 16 }, u64::from(kind.max(1)))
        };
        let mut b = vec![0u8; (len * width) as usize];
        mem.read_exact_at(&mut b, o + at).ok()?;
        Some(match width {
            1 => b.iter().map(|&c| c as char).collect(),
            2 => String::from_utf16_lossy(&b.chunks(2).map(|c| u16::from_le_bytes([c[0], c[1]])).collect::<Vec<_>>()),
            _ => b.chunks(4).filter_map(|c| char::from_u32(u32::from_le_bytes(c.try_into().unwrap()))).collect(),
        })
    }

    /// An int's digits (30 bits each) and sign, as the version keeps them.
    fn int_value(&self, mem: &Mem, o: u64, ty: u64) -> Option<i64> {
        if self.ver.0 == 2 && ty == self.t.int {
            return word(mem, o + 16).map(|v| v as i64);
        }
        let (ndigits, negative) = if self.ver >= (3, 12) {
            let tag = word(mem, o + 16)?;
            (tag >> 3, tag & 3 == 2)
        } else {
            let size = word(mem, o + 16)? as i64;
            (size.unsigned_abs(), size < 0)
        };
        if ndigits > 2 {
            return None;
        }
        let mut v: i64 = 0;
        for i in 0..ndigits {
            v |= i64::from(half(mem, o + 24 + 4 * i)? & 0x3fff_ffff) << (30 * i);
        }
        Some(if negative { -v } else { v })
    }

    /// What an object is, for listing.
    fn val(&self, mem: &Mem, o: u64) -> Val {
        let Some(t) = self.type_of(mem, o) else { return Val::Other };
        if t == self.t.float {
            return word(mem, o + 16).map_or(Val::Other, |b| Val::Float(f64::from_bits(b)));
        }
        if t == self.t.bool_ {
            return Val::Other;
        }
        if t == self.t.int || (self.t.long != 0 && t == self.t.long) {
            return self.int_value(mem, o, t).map_or(Val::Other, Val::Int);
        }
        let flags = self.flags(mem, t);
        if flags & (DICT_SUBCLASS | LIST_SUBCLASS | TUPLE_SUBCLASS) != 0 || t == self.t.dict || t == self.t.store || flags & HEAPTYPE != 0 {
            return Val::Obj(o);
        }
        Val::Other
    }

    fn key(&self, mem: &Mem, k: u64) -> Option<Key> {
        if let Some(s) = self.text(mem, k) {
            return Some(Key::Name(s));
        }
        match self.val(mem, k) {
            Val::Int(i) => Some(Key::Index(i)),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// A dict's entries: each key with the object it holds and the slot holding it.
    fn dict_entries(&self, mem: &Mem, d: u64) -> Vec<(Key, u64, u64)> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let mut push = |k: u64, slot: u64| {
            if let (Some(v), Some(key)) = (word(mem, slot).filter(|&v| v != 0), (k != 0).then(|| self.key(mem, k)).flatten()) {
                out.push((key, v, slot));
            }
        };
        if self.ver.0 == 2 {
            let (Some(mask), Some(table)) = (word(mem, d + 32), word(mem, d + 40)) else { return out };
            let n = (mask + 1).min(MAX_ENTRIES);
            let mut b = vec![0u8; 24 * n as usize];
            if mem.read_exact_at(&mut b, table).is_err() {
                return out;
            }
            for i in 0..n as usize {
                let k = u64::from_le_bytes(b[24 * i + 8..24 * i + 16].try_into().unwrap());
                push(k, table + 24 * i as u64 + 16);
            }
            return out;
        }
        let (Some(keys), Some(values)) = (word(mem, d + 32), word(mem, d + 40)) else { return out };
        let Some((entries, n, unicode)) = self.keys_layout(mem, keys) else { return out };
        let values = if values != 0 && self.ver >= (3, 13) { values + 8 } else { values };
        let size = if unicode { 16 } else { 24 };
        for i in 0..n {
            let e = entries + size * i;
            let k = word(mem, if unicode { e } else { e + 8 }).unwrap_or(0);
            let slot = if values != 0 { values + 8 * i } else if unicode { e + 8 } else { e + 16 };
            push(k, slot);
        }
        out
    }

    /// A dict keys object's entries (address, count) and whether they're the short kind
    /// {key, value} (3.11+: tables of str keys only; earlier entries are {hash, key, value}).
    fn keys_layout(&self, mem: &Mem, keys: u64) -> Option<(u64, u64, bool)> {
        if self.ver >= (3, 11) {
            let mut b = [0u8; 32];
            mem.read_exact_at(&mut b, keys).ok()?;
            let (log2_index, kind) = (b[9], b[10]);
            let n = u64::from_le_bytes(b[24..32].try_into().unwrap());
            if log2_index > 32 || n > MAX_ENTRIES {
                return None;
            }
            Some((keys + 32 + (1u64 << log2_index), n, kind != 0))
        } else {
            let size = word(mem, keys + 8)?;
            let n = word(mem, keys + 32)?;
            if size > MAX_ENTRIES * 2 || n > MAX_ENTRIES {
                return None;
            }
            let ix = match size {
                0..=0xff => 1,
                0x100..=0xffff => 2,
                0x1_0000..=0xffff_ffff => 4,
                _ => 8,
            };
            Some((keys + 40 + size * ix, n, false))
        }
    }

    fn dict_get(&self, mem: &Mem, d: u64, key: &Key) -> Option<(u64, u64)> {
        self.dict_entries(mem, d).into_iter().find(|(k, _, _)| k == key).map(|(_, v, s)| (v, s))
    }

    /// Where a heap type keeps its shared keys (`ht_cached_keys`): after `ht_name` (a str
    /// equal to the class's name), `ht_slots` and `ht_qualname`.
    fn cached_keys(&self, mem: &Mem, t: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        let mut at = self.ht_name_at.lock().unwrap();
        if at.is_none() {
            let name = word(mem, t + TP_NAME).and_then(|n| cstr(mem, n))?;
            let short = name.rsplit('.').next().unwrap_or(&name).to_owned();
            *at = (400..1600).step_by(8).find(|&o| word(mem, t + o).and_then(|s| self.text(mem, s)).as_deref() == Some(short.as_str()));
        }
        word(mem, t + (*at)? + 24).filter(|&k| k != 0)
    }

    /// An object's attributes (its dict's entries, or its values named by its class's keys).
    fn attrs(&self, mem: &Mem, o: u64) -> Vec<(Key, u64, u64)> {
        let Some(t) = self.type_of(mem, o) else { return Vec::new() };
        let flags = self.flags(mem, t);
        let split = |values: u64| {
            let Some(keys) = self.cached_keys(mem, t) else { return Vec::new() };
            let Some((entries, n, unicode)) = self.keys_layout(mem, keys) else { return Vec::new() };
            let size = if unicode { 16 } else { 24 };
            (0..n)
                .filter_map(|i| {
                    let k = word(mem, entries + size * i + if unicode { 0 } else { 8 })?;
                    let slot = values + 8 * i;
                    let v = word(mem, slot).filter(|&v| v != 0)?;
                    Some((self.key(mem, k)?, v, slot))
                })
                .collect()
        };
        if self.ver >= (3, 11) && flags & MANAGED_DICT != 0 {
            let w = word(mem, o.wrapping_sub(24)).unwrap_or(0);
            return match self.ver {
                (3, 11) if w != 0 => self.dict_entries(mem, w),
                (3, 11) => word(mem, o.wrapping_sub(32)).filter(|&v| v != 0).map(split).unwrap_or_default(),
                (3, 12) if w & 1 == 1 => split(w + 1),
                (3, 12) => if w != 0 { self.dict_entries(mem, w) } else { Vec::new() },
                _ if w != 0 => self.dict_entries(mem, w),
                _ if flags & INLINE_VALUES != 0 => {
                    let values = o + word(mem, t + TP_BASICSIZE).unwrap_or(0);
                    if byte(mem, values + 3) == Some(1) { split(values + 8) } else { Vec::new() }
                }
                _ => Vec::new(),
            };
        }
        let off = word(mem, t + TP_DICTOFFSET).unwrap_or(0) as i64;
        if off > 0 {
            if let Some(d) = word(mem, o + off as u64).filter(|&d| d != 0 && self.is_dict(mem, d)) {
                return self.dict_entries(mem, d);
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }

    /// A list's or tuple's elements: index, object and slot.
    fn elements(&self, mem: &Mem, o: u64) -> Vec<(i64, u64, u64)> {
        let Some(t) = self.type_of(mem, o) else { return Vec::new() };
        let flags = self.flags(mem, t);
        let Some(n) = word(mem, o + 16).filter(|&n| n <= MAX_ENTRIES) else { return Vec::new() };
        let items = if flags & LIST_SUBCLASS != 0 || t == self.t.list {
            word(mem, o + 24).unwrap_or(0)
        } else if flags & TUPLE_SUBCLASS != 0 || t == self.t.tuple {
            o + 24
        } else {
            return Vec::new();
        };
        if items == 0 {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        (0..n.min(MAX_ELEMENTS)).filter_map(|i| Some((i as i64, word(mem, items + 8 * i).filter(|&v| v != 0)?, items + 8 * i))).collect()
    }

    /// An object's entries by name or index: a dict's, a list's or an object's attributes.
    fn children(&self, mem: &Mem, o: u64) -> Vec<(Key, u64, u64)> {
        if self.is_dict(mem, o) {
            return self.dict_entries(mem, o);
        }
        let el = self.elements(mem, o);
        if !el.is_empty() {
            return el.into_iter().map(|(i, v, s)| (Key::Index(i), v, s)).collect();
        }
        self.attrs(mem, o)
    }

    fn type_name(&self, mem: &Mem, o: u64) -> String {
        self.type_of(mem, o).and_then(|t| word(mem, t + TP_NAME)).and_then(|n| cstr(mem, n)).unwrap_or_default()
    }

    /// Reference count: the low 32 bits in 3.12+ (the rest are flags), the whole word before.
    fn refcount(&self, mem: &Mem, o: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        let w = word(mem, o)?;
        Some(if self.ver >= (3, 12) { w & 0xffff_ffff } else { w })
    }

    /// The cached small int for `v` (-5..256): the int objects next to the one for 0, found from
    /// any small int's place.
    fn small_int(&self, mem: &Mem, v: i64, near: Option<u64>) -> Option<u64> {
        if !(-5..=256).contains(&v) {
            return None;
        }
        let mut small = self.small.lock().unwrap();
        if small.is_none() {
            let o = near?;
            let ty = self.type_of(mem, o)?;
            let have = self.int_value(mem, o, ty)?;
            if !(-5..=256).contains(&have) {
                return None;
            }
            let size = if self.ver.0 == 2 { 24 } else { 32 };
            let zero = o.wrapping_add_signed(-have * size as i64);
            *small = Some((zero, size));
        }
        let (zero, size) = (*small)?;
        let at = zero.wrapping_add_signed(v * size as i64);
        let ty = self.type_of(mem, at)?;
        (ty == self.t.int && self.int_value(mem, at, ty) == Some(v)).then_some(at)
    }
}

/// The located game per pid (one game is attached at a time: the `py` value type reads through
/// the last one); a failed search is tried again after `RETRY`.
pub fn shared(heap: &Heap) -> Option<Arc<Py>> {
    const RETRY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);
    let mut found = FOUND.lock().unwrap();
    if let Some((pid, py, at)) = found.as_ref() {
        if *pid == heap.pid && (py.is_some() || at.elapsed() < RETRY) {
            return py.clone();
        }
    }
    let py = Py::locate(heap).map(Arc::new);
    *found = Some((heap.pid, py.clone(), Instant::now()));
    py
}

static FOUND: Mutex<Option<(u32, Option<Arc<Py>>, Instant)>> = Mutex::new(None);

fn current() -> Option<Arc<Py>> {
    FOUND.lock().unwrap().as_ref().and_then(|(_, py, _)| py.clone())
}

/// The number a slot's object holds now (the `py` value type).
pub fn read_slot(mem: &Mem, slot: u64) -> Option<f64> {
    let py = current()?;
    match py.val(mem, word(mem, slot)?) {
        Val::Int(i) => Some(i as f64),
        Val::Float(f) => Some(f),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Writes a number to the object a slot points to: in place when only that slot points to
/// it; a small int by pointing the slot to the cached one; else refused (the object is shared:
/// another variable, a constant of the game's code, Ren'Py's rollback log).
pub fn write_slot(mem: &Mem, slot: u64, v: f64) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let refused = |why: &str| Err(std::io::Error::other(why.to_owned()));
    let Some(py) = current() else { return refused("not a Python game") };
    let Some(o) = word(mem, slot) else { return refused("unreadable") };
    let Some(t) = py.type_of(mem, o) else { return refused("unreadable") };
    let own = py.refcount(mem, o) == Some(1);
    if t == py.t.float {
        if !own {
            return refused("the game shares this number with something else, not written");
        }
        return mem.write_all_at(&v.to_bits().to_le_bytes(), o + 16);
    }
    let is_int = t == py.t.int || (py.t.long != 0 && t == py.t.long);
    let Some(have) = is_int.then(|| py.int_value(mem, o, t)).flatten() else { return refused("not a Python number now") };
    let v = v.round() as i64;
    if v == have {
        return Ok(());
    }
    if own && !(-5..=256).contains(&have) {
        if py.ver.0 == 2 && t == py.t.int {
            return mem.write_all_at(&v.to_le_bytes(), o + 16);
        }
        // 30-bit digits, as many as the object has room for (a value never grows it).
        let ndigits = if py.ver >= (3, 12) { word(mem, o + 16).unwrap_or(0) >> 3 } else { (word(mem, o + 16).unwrap_or(0) as i64).unsigned_abs() };
        let mag = v.unsigned_abs();
        let need = match mag {
            0 => 0,
            m if m < 1 << 30 => 1,
            m if m < 1 << 60 => 2,
            _ => 3,
        };
        if need > ndigits {
            return refused("the number doesn't fit the game's number object, not written");
        }
        for i in 0..need {
            mem.write_all_at(&(((mag >> (30 * i)) & 0x3fff_ffff) as u32).to_le_bytes(), o + 24 + 4 * i)?;
        }
        let head = if py.ver >= (3, 12) {
            (need << 3) | if v == 0 { 1 } else if v < 0 { 2 } else { 0 }
        } else {
            (if v < 0 { -(need as i64) } else { need as i64 }) as u64
        };
        return mem.write_all_at(&head.to_le_bytes(), o + 16);
    }
    // Shared (small ints, constants): point the slot to the cached small int.
    let Some(target) = py.small_int(mem, v, (-5..=256).contains(&have).then_some(o)) else {
        return refused("the game shares this number object (a small number or a constant of its code): only -5 to 256 can be set now; it can be set once the game changes it");
    };
    if py.ver < (3, 12) {
        // Not immortal before 3.12: the slot's new reference is counted (a small int is held
        // by thousands, a count one off never frees it).
        let Some(n) = word(mem, target).filter(|&n| n > 100) else { return refused("not written") };
        mem.write_all_at(&(n + 1).to_le_bytes(), target)?;
    }
    mem.write_all_at(&target.to_le_bytes(), slot)
}

/// One step of a path: a name (a dict key or an attribute) or an index (a list's element or a
/// dict's int key).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
enum Step {
    Name(String),
    Index(i64),
}

/// A saved path from a namespace to a number.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct PyPath {
    root: String,
    steps: Vec<Step>,
}

fn encode(name: &str) -> String {
    name.chars()
        .map(|c| match c {
            'a'..='z' | 'A'..='Z' | '0'..='9' | '_' => c.to_string(),
            _ => c.to_string().bytes().map(|b| format!("%{b:02X}")).collect(),
        })
        .collect()
}

fn decode(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    let mut it = text.bytes();
    while let Some(b) = it.next() {
        if b == b'%' {
            let hex = [it.next()?, it.next()?];
            bytes.push(u8::from_str_radix(std::str::from_utf8(&hex).ok()?, 16).ok()?);
        } else {
            bytes.push(b);
        }
    }
    String::from_utf8(bytes).ok()
}

impl PyPath {
    /// "py:<namespace>#<name>[.<name>|[i]]...".
    pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Option<PyPath> {
        let (root, mut rest) = text.strip_prefix("py:")?.split_once('#')?;
        if root.is_empty() || rest.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let mut steps = Vec::new();
        let mut first = true;
        while !rest.is_empty() {
            let (sep, body) = match rest.as_bytes()[0] {
                b'.' | b'[' => (rest.as_bytes()[0], &rest[1..]),
                _ if first => (b'.', rest),
                _ => return None,
            };
            first = false;
            if sep == b'[' {
                let (n, after) = body.split_once(']')?;
                steps.push(Step::Index(n.parse().ok()?));
                rest = after;
                continue;
            }
            let end = body.find(['.', '[']).unwrap_or(body.len());
            let name = decode(&body[..end])?;
            if name.is_empty() {
                return None;
            }
            steps.push(Step::Name(name));
            rest = &body[end..];
        }
        Some(PyPath { root: root.to_owned(), steps })
    }

    pub fn text(&self) -> String {
        format!("py:{}#{}", self.root, self.steps_text(true))
    }

    fn steps_text(&self, encoded: bool) -> String {
        let mut t = String::new();
        for s in &self.steps {
            match s {
                Step::Name(n) => {
                    if !t.is_empty() {
                        t.push('.');
                    }
                    t += &if encoded { encode(n) } else { n.clone() };
                }
                Step::Index(i) => t += &format!("[{i}]"),
            }
        }
        t
    }

    /// As the list shows it: `player.hp`, a module's other than the game's own with its
    /// module's name (`settings.WIDTH`).
    fn shown(&self) -> String {
        let s = self.steps_text(false);
        match (self.root.as_str(), s.is_empty()) {
            ("__main__" | "store", _) => s,
            (r, true) => r.to_owned(),
            (r, false) => format!("{r}.{s}"),
        }
    }

    pub fn describe(&self) -> String {
        match self.root.as_str() {
            "store" => format!("{} among the game's Ren'Py variables", self.shown()),
            _ => format!("{} in the game's Python objects", self.shown()),
        }
    }

    fn then(&self, s: Step) -> PyPath {
        let mut p = self.clone();
        p.steps.push(s);
        p
    }

    fn last_name(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        self.steps.iter().rev().find_map(|s| match s {
            Step::Name(n) => Some(n.as_str()),
            _ => None,
        })
    }

    /// The path up to its first field named like the player itself.
    fn player_part(&self) -> Option<PyPath> {
        let i = self.steps.iter().position(|s| matches!(s, Step::Name(n) if the_player(n)))?;
        Some(PyPath { root: self.root.clone(), steps: self.steps[..=i].to_vec() })
    }

    /// Through how something looks or sounds (`player.image`, `player.rect`).
    fn presentation(&self) -> bool {
        const WORDS: &[&str] = &["sprite", "image", "surface", "rect", "font", "sound", "music", "anim", "frame", "texture", "screen", "mask", "particle", "camera", "clock"];
        self.steps.iter().any(|s| matches!(s, Step::Name(n) if WORDS.iter().any(|w| n.to_ascii_lowercase().contains(w))))
    }
}

/// Whether a name is the player itself (`player`, `hero`, `self_player`...): its whole name.
fn the_player(name: &str) -> bool {
    let n: String = name.chars().filter(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric()).collect::<String>().to_ascii_lowercase();
    ["player", "hero", "localplayer", "theplayer", "mainplayer", "playerchar", "playercharacter", "character", "maincharacter", "avatar", "protagonist", "mc", "pc", "ship", "playership"].contains(&n.as_str())
}

/// Constants by convention (`WIDTH`, `MAX_HP`).
fn constant(name: &str) -> bool {
    name.len() > 1 && name.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_uppercase() || c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '_') && name.chars().any(|c| c.is_ascii_uppercase())
}

/// The namespace the path starts from.
pub fn find_roots(heap: &Heap, path: &PyPath) -> Vec<u64> {
    let Some(py) = shared(heap) else { return Vec::new() };
    let mem = heap.mem();
    let found = py.roots.lock().unwrap().0.get(&path.root).copied();
    if let Some(d) = found.filter(|&d| py.is_dict(mem, d)) {
        return vec![d];
    }
    // Modules are imported as the game goes: look again (at most every 2 s).
    if py.roots.lock().unwrap().1.elapsed() >= Duration::from_secs(2) {
        py.find_roots(heap);
    }
    let found = py.roots.lock().unwrap().0.get(&path.root).copied();
    found.into_iter().collect()
}

/// Where the path leads: the slot pointing to the number, while it holds one.
pub fn walk(heap: &Heap, roots: &[u64], path: &PyPath) -> Vec<u64> {
    let Some(py) = shared(heap) else { return Vec::new() };
    let mem = heap.mem();
    roots
        .iter()
        .filter(|&&d| py.is_dict(mem, d))
        .filter_map(|&d| {
            let mut cur = d;
            let mut slot = 0;
            for s in &path.steps {
                let key = match s {
                    Step::Name(n) => Key::Name(n.clone()),
                    Step::Index(i) => Key::Index(*i),
                };
                let (v, at) = py.children(mem, cur).into_iter().find(|(k, _, _)| *k == key).map(|(_, v, s)| (v, s))?;
                cur = v;
                slot = at;
            }
            matches!(py.val(mem, cur), Val::Int(_) | Val::Float(_)).then_some(slot)
        })
        .collect()
}

/// A namespace or object whose numbers are listed.
struct Group {
    path: PyPath,
    class: String,
    numbers: Vec<(String, u64, PyPath)>,
}

/// Namespaces listed: the game's (`__main__`, Ren'Py's `store`, modules with no file or one
/// outside Python's and Ren'Py's own folders), not Python's or the engine's.
fn game_roots(py: &Py, mem: &Mem) -> Vec<(String, u64)> {
    let roots = py.roots.lock().unwrap().0.clone();
    let mut out: Vec<(String, u64)> = roots
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|(name, d)| {
            if name == "__main__" || name == "store" {
                return true;
            }
            if name.starts_with("store.") {
                return !name[6..].starts_with('_') && !["gui", "layeredimage", "updater", "iap", "icon", "achievement", "director", "build", "config"].contains(&&name[6..]);
            }
            if name.starts_with('_') || name.starts_with("renpy") || name.starts_with("pygame") || name.starts_with("encodings") {
                return false;
            }
            let file = py.dict_get(mem, *d, &Key::Name("__file__".into())).and_then(|(v, _)| py.text(mem, v));
            match file {
                None => false,
                Some(f) => !["/lib/python", "site-packages", "dist-packages", "/lib/py", "pythonlib", "/renpy/", ".zip/", "/usr/lib"].iter().any(|p| f.contains(p)),
            }
        })
        .collect();
    out.sort_by_key(|(n, _)| (n != "store" && n != "__main__", n.clone()));
    out
}

/// Every number reachable from the game's namespaces, breadth first (paths through the player
/// first: `game_roots`' `player` before its UI), each object by its shortest path.
fn groups(heap: &Heap) -> Option<Vec<Group>> {
    let py = shared(heap)?;
    let mem = heap.mem();
    if py.roots.lock().unwrap().1.elapsed() >= Duration::from_secs(2) {
        py.find_roots(heap);
    }
    let mut queues: [VecDeque<(u64, PyPath, usize)>; 2] = [VecDeque::new(), VecDeque::new()];
    let queue_of = |p: &PyPath| usize::from(p.player_part().is_none());
    for (name, d) in game_roots(&py, mem) {
        queues[1].push_back((d, PyPath { root: name, steps: Vec::new() }, 0));
    }
    let mut seen: HashSet<u64> = HashSet::new();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let (mut visited, mut listed) = (0, 0);
    while let Some((o, path, depth)) = queues[0].pop_front().or_else(|| queues[1].pop_front()) {
        if !seen.insert(o) {
            continue;
        }
        visited += 1;
        if visited > MAX_VISITED || listed > MAX_LISTED {
            break;
        }
        let mut g = Group { path: path.clone(), class: py.type_name(mem, o), numbers: Vec::new() };
        for (k, v, slot) in py.children(mem, o) {
            let step = match &k {
                Key::Name(n) if n.starts_with("__") => continue,
                Key::Name(n) => Step::Name(n.clone()),
                Key::Index(i) => Step::Index(*i),
            };
            match py.val(mem, v) {
                Val::Int(_) | Val::Float(_) => {
                    let label = match &k {
                        Key::Name(n) => n.clone(),
                        Key::Index(i) => format!("[{i}]"),
                    };
                    g.numbers.push((label, slot, path.then(step)));
                }
                Val::Obj(x) if depth < MAX_DEPTH && !seen.contains(&x) => {
                    let p = path.then(step);
                    queues[queue_of(&p)].push_back((x, p, depth + 1));
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        if !g.numbers.is_empty() {
            listed += g.numbers.len();
            out.push(g);
        }
    }
    Some(out)
}

/// The Browse tab's list for a Python game: the game's variables (Ren'Py's store, a pygame
/// game's globals), the player's object and what's in it, then (`more`) everything else.
pub fn player(heap: &Heap) -> Option<Vec<ListedObject>> {
    let groups = groups(heap)?;
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for g in groups {
        let fields = |nums: Vec<(String, u64, PyPath)>| nums.into_iter().map(|(label, addr, _)| Listed { label, addr, kind: "py" }).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        if g.path.steps.is_empty() {
            let word = match g.path.root.as_str() {
                "store" => Some("@variables"),
                "__main__" => Some("@global"),
                _ => None,
            };
            let (consts, vars): (Vec<_>, Vec<_>) = g.numbers.into_iter().partition(|n| constant(&n.0));
            let name = word.map_or(g.path.root.clone(), str::to_owned);
            out.push(ListedObject { name: name.clone(), class: "module".into(), role: "game", owner: None, more: word.is_none(), fields: fields(vars) });
            out.push(ListedObject { name: format!("{} ({})", g.path.root, "constants"), class: "module".into(), role: "game", owner: None, more: true, fields: fields(consts) });
            continue;
        }
        let player = (g.path.last_name().is_some_and(the_player) || the_player(&g.class)) && !g.path.presentation();
        let owner = g.path.player_part().filter(|p| !player && *p != g.path && !g.path.presentation()).map(|p| p.shown());
        let main = player || owner.is_some() || g.numbers.iter().any(|n| player_like(&n.0) && !constant(&n.0)) && g.path.steps.len() == 1;
        out.push(ListedObject {
            name: g.path.shown(),
            class: g.class,
            role: if player { "character" } else if owner.is_some() { "part" } else { "game" },
            owner,
            more: !main,
            fields: fields(g.numbers),
        });
    }
    out.retain(|o| !o.fields.is_empty());
    out.sort_by_key(|o| (o.more, o.role != "character" && o.class != "module"));
    Some(out)
}

/// The path to a number the list has (its slot's address), checked by following it.
pub fn discover(heap: &Heap, target: u64) -> Option<(PyPath, Vec<u64>)> {
    let path = groups(heap)?.into_iter().flat_map(|g| g.numbers).find(|n| n.1 == target)?.2;
    let leads = walk(heap, &find_roots(heap, &path), &path);
    leads.contains(&target).then_some((path, leads))
}

/// pydump [path]: the game's Python as Ferret reads it (version, types, namespaces), or what a
/// path leads to (a namespace's or object's entries).
pub fn diagnose(heap: &Heap, at: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let t = Instant::now();
    let Some(py) = shared(heap) else { return vec!["no Python objects found (only 64-bit CPython 2.7 and 3.x)".into()] };
    let mem = heap.mem();
    let roots = py.roots.lock().unwrap().0.clone();
    let mut out = vec![format!("Python {}.{}, {} namespaces, str at +{}, types {:x?} ({} ms)", py.ver.0, py.ver.1, roots.len(), py.str_at, py.t, t.elapsed().as_millis())];
    let _ = py.pid;
    if at.is_empty() {
        let mut names: Vec<String> = game_roots(&py, mem).into_iter().map(|(n, _)| n).collect();
        names.truncate(80);
        out.push(format!("game namespaces: {}", names.join(" ")));
        return out;
    }
    let text = if at.contains('#') { format!("py:{at}") } else { format!("py:{at}#x") };
    let Some(mut p) = PyPath::parse(&text) else { return vec!["bad path".into()] };
    if !at.contains('#') {
        p.steps.clear();
    }
    let Some(&root) = roots.get(&p.root) else { return vec![format!("{}: no such namespace", p.root)] };
    let mut cur = root;
    for s in &p.steps {
        let key = match s {
            Step::Name(n) => Key::Name(n.clone()),
            Step::Index(i) => Key::Index(*i),
        };
        let Some((_, v, _)) = py.children(mem, cur).into_iter().find(|(k, _, _)| *k == key) else { return vec![format!("{at}: not found")] };
        cur = v;
    }
    out.push(format!("{} at {cur:#x}", py.type_name(mem, cur)));
    for (k, v, slot) in py.children(mem, cur) {
        let shown = match py.val(mem, v) {
            Val::Int(i) => format!("{i} (refs {})", py.refcount(mem, v).unwrap_or(0)),
            Val::Float(f) => format!("{f} (refs {})", py.refcount(mem, v).unwrap_or(0)),
            _ => py.text(mem, v).map(|s| format!("{s:?}")).unwrap_or_else(|| py.type_name(mem, v)),
        };
        out.push(format!("{k:?} = {shown} @{slot:#x}"));
    }
    out
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn paths_read_back() {
        for text in ["py:store#souls", "py:__main__#player.hp", "py:__main__#party[0].hp", "py:game.state#a%20b.c", "py:__main__#grid[1][2]"] {
            assert_eq!(PyPath::parse(text).unwrap().text(), text, "{text}");
        }
        let p = PyPath::parse("py:__main__#party[2].stats.hp").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(p.steps, vec![Step::Name("party".into()), Step::Index(2), Step::Name("stats".into()), Step::Name("hp".into())]);
        assert_eq!(p.shown(), "party[2].stats.hp");
        assert_eq!(PyPath::parse("py:settings#WIDTH").unwrap().shown(), "settings.WIDTH");
        assert!(PyPath::parse("py:store").is_none());
        assert!(PyPath::parse("py:store#").is_none());
        assert!(PyPath::parse("py:#x").is_none());
        assert!(PyPath::parse("py:store#a..b").is_none());
        assert!(PyPath::parse("py:store#a[x]").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn names() {
        assert!(the_player("player") && the_player("Hero") && the_player("main_character") && !the_player("players_score"));
        assert!(constant("WIDTH") && !constant("hp"));
    }
}
```

`helper/src/steam.rs`:

```rs
// What Steam knows about a game (appcache/appinfo.vdf): its name, whether it uses Valve
// Anti-Cheat, whether it's played with other people (an MMO always is) and whether it has
// Steam's online leaderboards.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fs::File;
use crate::mem::FileAt;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Mutex;
use std::time::SystemTime;

#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct App {
    pub name: String,
    pub vac: bool,
    pub multiplayer: bool,
    pub single_player: bool,
    pub mmo: bool,
    pub leaderboards: bool,
}

impl App {
    /// Played only with other people: an MMO, or not listed as single-player.
    pub fn online_only(&self) -> bool {
        self.mmo || self.multiplayer && !self.single_player
    }
}

/// Store categories: 2 = Single-player, 8 = Valve Anti-Cheat enabled; 1 = Multi-player,
/// 20 = MMO, 36 = Online PvP, 38 = Online Co-op; 25 = Steam Leaderboards.
const SINGLE_PLAYER: &str = "category_2";
const VAC: &str = "category_8";
const LEADERBOARDS: &str = "category_25";
const MMO: &str = "category_20";
const MULTIPLAYER: &[&str] = &["category_1", "category_20", "category_36", "category_38"];

/// The games list asks every second: answers are kept until appinfo.vdf changes.
static CACHE: Mutex<Option<HashMap<(PathBuf, u32), (SystemTime, Option<App>)>>> = Mutex::new(None);

/// `steam` = the Steam folder the game was started from (STEAM_COMPAT_CLIENT_INSTALL_PATH).
pub fn app(steam: Option<&str>, id: u32) -> Option<App> {
    let home = PathBuf::from(std::env::var_os("HOME").unwrap_or_default());
    let usual = [".local/share/Steam", ".steam/steam", ".var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/.local/share/Steam"];
    let roots = steam.map(PathBuf::from).into_iter().chain(usual.iter().map(|d| home.join(d)));
    for root in roots {
        let path = root.join("appcache/appinfo.vdf");
        let Ok(mtime) = path.metadata().and_then(|m| m.modified()) else { continue };
        let mut cache = CACHE.lock().unwrap();
        let cache = cache.get_or_insert_with(HashMap::new);
        let key = (path, id);
        match cache.get(&key) {
            Some((t, app)) if *t == mtime => return app.clone(),
            _ => {}
        }
        let app = read(&key.0, id);
        cache.insert(key, (mtime, app.clone()));
        return app;
    }
    None
}

/// Entries are <app id> <size> <header> <binary key-values>, ending with app id 0. Version 29
/// keeps the key names in a string table at the end (its offset follows the magic).
fn read(path: &Path, id: u32) -> Option<App> {
    let f = File::open(path).ok()?;
    let bytes = |off: u64, n: usize| {
        let mut b = vec![0; n];
        f.read_exact_at(&mut b, off).ok().map(|_| b)
    };
    let u32_at = |off: u64| bytes(off, 4).map(|b| u32::from_le_bytes(b.try_into().unwrap()));
    let (mut off, header, indexed) = match u32_at(0)? {
        0x0756_4427 => (8, 40, false),
        0x0756_4428 => (8, 60, false),
        0x0756_4429 => (16, 60, true),
        _ => return None,
    };
    loop {
        let (app, size) = (u32_at(off)?, u64::from(u32_at(off + 4)?));
        if app == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        if app == id {
            let data = bytes(off + 8 + header, size.checked_sub(header)? as usize)?;
            let table = if indexed { strings(&f)? } else { Vec::new() };
            return parse(&data, indexed.then_some(&table[..]));
        }
        off += 8 + size;
    }
}

fn strings(f: &File) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
    let mut b = [0; 8];
    f.read_exact_at(&mut b, 8).ok()?;
    let start = u64::from_le_bytes(b);
    let len = f.metadata().ok()?.len().checked_sub(start)?;
    let mut data = vec![0; len as usize];
    f.read_exact_at(&mut data, start).ok()?;
    let count = u32::from_le_bytes(data.get(..4)?.try_into().ok()?) as usize;
    Some(data[4..].split(|b| *b == 0).take(count).map(|s| String::from_utf8_lossy(s).into_owned()).collect())
}

/// Walks the key-values: type byte, key (table index or C string), value; 0 opens a
/// section and 8 closes one.
fn parse(d: &[u8], table: Option<&[String]>) -> Option<App> {
    let mut p = 0;
    let cstr = |p: &mut usize| {
        let end = *p + d.get(*p..)?.iter().position(|b| *b == 0)?;
        let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&d[*p..end]).into_owned();
        *p = end + 1;
        Some(s)
    };
    let mut path: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut app = App::default();
    loop {
        let t = *d.get(p)?;
        p += 1;
        if t == 8 {
            if path.pop().is_none() {
                return Some(app);
            }
            continue;
        }
        let key = match table {
            Some(table) => {
                let i = u32::from_le_bytes(d.get(p..p + 4)?.try_into().ok()?) as usize;
                p += 4;
                table.get(i)?.clone()
            }
            None => cstr(&mut p)?,
        };
        let at = |want: &[&str]| path.iter().map(String::as_str).eq(want.iter().copied());
        if at(&["appinfo", "common", "category"]) {
            app.vac |= key == VAC;
            app.single_player |= key == SINGLE_PLAYER;
            app.mmo |= key == MMO;
            app.leaderboards |= key == LEADERBOARDS;
            app.multiplayer |= MULTIPLAYER.contains(&key.as_str());
        }
        match t {
            0 => path.push(key),
            1 => {
                let s = cstr(&mut p)?;
                if at(&["appinfo", "common"]) && key == "name" {
                    app.name = s;
                }
            }
            2 | 3 | 4 | 6 => p += 4,
            7 | 10 => p += 8,
            _ => return None,
        }
    }
}

```

`helper/src/trace.rs`:

```rs
// Hardware breakpoints on every thread of the game: "which instructions access this address"
// and "what is in the registers when this instruction runs". Nothing is written into the
// game's code. Setting them is the OS's part (`Tracer`: ptrace on Linux, the debugger API on
// Windows); working out the instruction is the same everywhere.

#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
#[path = "trace_linux.rs"]
mod tracer;
#[cfg(windows)]
#[path = "trace_windows.rs"]
mod tracer;
pub use tracer::*;

pub const DR7_ACCESS_4: u64 = 1 | (3 << 16) | (3 << 18);
pub const DR7_ACCESS_2: u64 = 1 | (3 << 16) | (1 << 18);
pub const DR7_EXECUTE: u64 = 1;

/// Debug status bits of breakpoints 0-3: set when one of ours fired.
const DR6_HITS: u64 = 0xf;

/// A thread's registers at a breakpoint: the general ones in x86 encoding order (eax/rax,
/// ecx, ... r15), the instruction pointer, and whether it ran 64-bit code.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default, Debug)]
pub struct Regs {
    pub gpr: [u64; 16],
    pub rip: u64,
    pub is64: bool,
}

pub struct Hit {
    pub regs: Regs,
    /// Which breakpoint fired (0-3, as armed).
    pub slot: usize,
}

/// Register number (x86 encoding order) to its value.
pub fn reg(regs: &Regs, n: u8) -> u64 {
    regs.gpr[(n & 15) as usize]
}

/// Saved in profiles; r8 to r15 only exist in 64-bit code.
pub const REG_NAMES: [&str; 16] =
    ["eax", "ecx", "edx", "ebx", "esp", "ebp", "esi", "edi", "r8", "r9", "r10", "r11", "r12", "r13", "r14", "r15"];

/// Whether the thread was running 64-bit code.
pub fn is_64bit(regs: &Regs) -> bool {
    regs.is64
}

/// A memory access of the form [base register + displacement] (displacement may be 0). For
/// [base + index * scale + displacement] the displacement is where it went from the base this
/// time (target - base): arrays indexed by item type keep each item at its own place in the
/// object (Quake II's `client->pers.inventory[item]`, `dec [rcx+rax*4+0x2e8]`), so the same
/// instruction finds this item again from the object.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Access {
    pub start: u64,
    pub len: usize,
    pub base: u8,
    pub disp: i64,
}

// Opcodes with a ModRM byte, and the size of the immediate that follows the displacement.
fn one_byte_opcode(op: u8) -> Option<usize> {
    match op {
        0x01 | 0x03 | 0x09 | 0x0B | 0x11 | 0x13 | 0x19 | 0x1B | 0x21 | 0x23 | 0x29 | 0x2B | 0x31 | 0x33 | 0x39
        | 0x3B | 0x63 | 0x85 | 0x87 | 0x89 | 0x8B | 0x8D | 0xFF => Some(0),
        // x87: fld/fst/fadd/fcomp ... on floats (D8, D9) and doubles (DC, DD), integers (DA, DB, DE, DF).
        0xD8..=0xDF => Some(0),
        0x83 | 0x6B | 0xC1 => Some(1),
        0x81 | 0xC7 | 0x69 => Some(4),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Works out the instruction that ends at `after` (a data breakpoint stops
/// right after the accessing instruction) and accessed `target`.
/// `code` holds the bytes from `code_addr`.
/// In 64-bit code a 0x4x byte before the opcode may be a REX prefix or the end of the previous
/// instruction, so this returns every reading that fits, the REX one first; only the real start
/// runs (an execute breakpoint tells them apart).
pub fn decode_access(code: &[u8], code_addr: u64, after: u64, target: u64, regs: &Regs) -> Vec<Access> {
    let end = (after - code_addr) as usize;
    let is64 = is_64bit(regs);
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    // (displacement size, ModRM mode): [reg+disp32], [reg+disp8], [reg]
    for (disp_size, want_mode) in [(4usize, 2u8), (1, 1), (0, 0)] {
        for sib in [false, true] {
            for imm in [0usize, 1, 4] {
                let Some(disp_start) = end.checked_sub(imm + disp_size) else { continue };
                let Some(modrm_at) = disp_start.checked_sub(1 + sib as usize) else { continue };
                let modrm = code[modrm_at];
                let (mode, rm) = (modrm >> 6, modrm & 7);
                if mode != want_mode || ((rm == 4) != sib) {
                    continue;
                }
                // Mode 0 with rm 5 is an absolute (32-bit) or RIP-relative (64-bit) address.
                if mode == 0 && rm == 5 {
                    continue;
                }
                let sib_byte = sib.then(|| code[disp_start - 1]);
                if let Some(s) = sib_byte {
                    // Mode 0 with SIB base 5 has no base register, only a disp32.
                    if mode == 0 && s & 7 == 5 {
                        continue;
                    }
                }
                let low_base = sib_byte.map_or(rm, |s| s & 7);
                let d = &code[disp_start..disp_start + disp_size];
                let disp = match disp_size {
                    4 => i32::from_le_bytes([d[0], d[1], d[2], d[3]]) as i64,
                    1 => d[0] as i8 as i64,
                    _ => 0,
                };
                let Some(mut op_start) = modrm_at.checked_sub(1) else { continue };
                let op = code[op_start];
                let two_byte = op_start >= 1 && code[op_start - 1] == 0x0F;
                let imm_ok = if two_byte {
                    op_start -= 1;
                    imm == 0
                } else {
                    // 0x63 is movsxd (a 32-bit value into a 64-bit register, Mono's JIT) only in
                    // 64-bit code.
                    one_byte_opcode(op) == Some(imm) && (op != 0x63 || is64)
                };
                if !imm_ok {
                    continue;
                }
                // A REX prefix sits right before the opcode: B extends the base register, X the
                // SIB index, R the ModRM reg field.
                let maybe_rex = is64 && op_start >= 1 && (0x40..=0x4F).contains(&code[op_start - 1]);
                let rexes: &[u8] = if maybe_rex { &[code[op_start - 1], 0] } else { &[0] };
                let mut matched = Vec::new();
                let mut clobbered = Vec::new();
                for &rex in rexes {
                    // SIB index 4 without REX.X means no index register.
                    let index = sib_byte.map(|s| (s >> 3) & 7 | (rex & 2) << 2).filter(|&i| i != 4);
                    let scale = sib_byte.map_or(1, |s| 1u64 << (s >> 6));
                    let base = low_base | (rex & 1) << 3;
                    // A REX prefix must come last, so only operand-size/SSE prefixes can precede it.
                    // (A 0x4x byte before those is the end of the previous instruction.)
                    let mut start = op_start - (rex != 0) as usize;
                    let mut legacy = 0;
                    while start > 0 && legacy < 2 && matches!(code[start - 1], 0x66 | 0xF2 | 0xF3) {
                        start -= 1;
                        legacy += 1;
                    }
                    let dest = (modrm >> 3) & 7 | (rex & 4) << 1;
                    // Loads into a register: it holds the value afterwards, not what it held.
                    let loads = |r: u8| dest == r && if two_byte { matches!(op, 0xB6 | 0xB7 | 0xBE | 0xBF) } else { matches!(op, 0x8B | 0x63) };
                    let low = |a: u64| a & 0xFFFF_FFFF;
                    let from_base = target.wrapping_sub(reg(regs, base)) as i64;
                    let (hits, disp) = match index {
                        None => (low(reg(regs, base).wrapping_add(disp as u64)) == low(target), disp),
                        Some(i) => {
                            let step = from_base.wrapping_sub(disp);
                            let fits = step.rem_euclid(scale as i64) == 0 && step.unsigned_abs() < 1 << 24;
                            // A loaded-over index can't be checked; the rest of the address can.
                            let same = loads(i) || low(reg(regs, i).wrapping_mul(scale).wrapping_add(disp as u64)) == low(step.wrapping_add(disp) as u64);
                            (fits && same && !loads(base), from_base)
                        }
                    };
                    let access = Access { start: code_addr + start as u64, len: end - start, base, disp };
                    if hits {
                        matched.push(access);
                    } else if index.is_none() && !two_byte && matches!(op, 0x8B | 0x63) && dest == base {
                        // `mov reg, [reg+disp]` (or movsxd) overwrites its own base register.
                        clobbered.push(access);
                    }
                }
                if !matched.is_empty() {
                    return matched;
                }
                if found.is_empty() {
                    found = clobbered;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    found
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn byte_before_opcode_is_not_always_rex() {
        // mov edx,[rsp+0x4c]; mov eax,[rax+0xc] -- the 0x4c is not a REX prefix of the second.
        let code = [0x48, 0x8b, 0x05, 0xbd, 0x64, 0x00, 0x00, 0x8b, 0x54, 0x24, 0x4c, 0x8b, 0x40, 0x0c];
        let mut regs = Regs::default();
        regs.is64 = true;
        regs.gpr[0] = 1234; // the loaded value: the base is gone
        let after = 0x1000 + code.len() as u64;
        let found = decode_access(&code, 0x1000, after, 0x5000_000c, &regs);
        assert_eq!(found, vec![Access { start: 0x100b, len: 3, base: 0, disp: 12 }]);

        // mov ecx,[rax+0xc] after the same bytes: both readings hit the target.
        let code = [0x8b, 0x54, 0x24, 0x4c, 0x8b, 0x48, 0x0c];
        regs.gpr[0] = 0x5000_0000;
        let found = decode_access(&code, 0x1000, 0x1007, 0x5000_000c, &regs);
        let starts: Vec<u64> = found.iter().map(|a| a.start).collect();
        assert_eq!(starts, vec![0x1003, 0x1004]);

        // 32-bit code has no REX prefixes.
        regs.is64 = false;
        let found = decode_access(&code, 0x1000, 0x1007, 0x5000_000c, &regs);
        assert_eq!(found, vec![Access { start: 0x1004, len: 3, base: 0, disp: 12 }]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn movsxd() {
        // Valheim (64-bit Mono): mov rax,[rbp-0x238]; movsxd rax,[rax+0x38] -- loads over its base.
        let code = [0x48, 0x8b, 0x85, 0xc8, 0xfd, 0xff, 0xff, 0x48, 0x63, 0x40, 0x38];
        let mut regs = Regs::default();
        regs.is64 = true;
        regs.gpr[0] = 21;
        let found = decode_access(&code, 0x1000, 0x100b, 0x7f00_0000_0038, &regs);
        let starts: Vec<u64> = found.iter().map(|a| a.start).collect();
        assert_eq!(starts, vec![0x1007, 0x1008]);

        // movsxd rax,[rbx+0x38]
        let code = [0x3b, 0xc1, 0x7c, 0x07, 0x48, 0x63, 0x43, 0x38];
        regs.gpr[3] = 0x7f00_0000_0000;
        let found = decode_access(&code, 0x1000, 0x1008, 0x7f00_0000_0038, &regs);
        assert_eq!(found[0], Access { start: 0x1004, len: 4, base: 3, disp: 0x38 });

        // 0x63 is arpl in 32-bit code.
        regs.is64 = false;
        assert!(decode_access(&code, 0x1000, 0x1008, 0x7f00_0000_0038, &regs).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn indexed() {
        // Quake II RTX firing the shotgun: movsxd rax,[rcx+0xdc8]; dec dword [rcx+rax*4+0x2e8]
        // (the shells in client->pers.inventory[item]): kept as the place from the object.
        let code = [0x48, 0x63, 0x81, 0xc8, 0x0d, 0x00, 0x00, 0xff, 0x8c, 0x81, 0xe8, 0x02, 0x00, 0x00];
        let mut regs = Regs::default();
        regs.is64 = true;
        regs.gpr[1] = 0x24b_0000;
        regs.gpr[0] = 7;
        let target = 0x24b_0000 + 0x2e8 + 7 * 4;
        let found = decode_access(&code, 0x1000, 0x100e, target, &regs);
        assert_eq!(found, vec![Access { start: 0x1007, len: 7, base: 1, disp: 0x2e8 + 28 }]);

        // Another index reaches another place: not this one.
        regs.gpr[0] = 8;
        assert!(decode_access(&code, 0x1000, 0x100e, target, &regs).is_empty());

        // movzx eax, word [rdx+rax*4+0x2e8] loads over its index: the rest still has to fit.
        let code = [0x0f, 0xb7, 0x84, 0x82, 0xe8, 0x02, 0x00, 0x00];
        regs.gpr[2] = 0x24b_0000;
        regs.gpr[0] = 0x55;
        let found = decode_access(&code, 0x1000, 0x1008, target, &regs);
        assert_eq!(found, vec![Access { start: 0x1000, len: 8, base: 2, disp: 0x2e8 + 28 }]);
        assert!(decode_access(&code, 0x1000, 0x1008, target + 2, &regs).is_empty());
    }
}
```

`helper/src/trace_linux.rs`:

```rs
// The tracer on Linux: debug registers set through ptrace on every thread of the game.

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::fs;
use std::io;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use super::{Hit, Regs, DR6_HITS, DR7_EXECUTE};

/// offsetof(struct user, u_debugreg) on x86_64.
const DEBUGREG: usize = 848;

pub struct Tracer {
    tids: Vec<i32>,
    // Threads we left stopped at a breakpoint; they need no interrupt before detaching.
    parked: HashSet<i32>,
}

fn ptrace(req: libc::c_uint, tid: i32, addr: usize, data: usize) -> libc::c_long {
    unsafe { libc::ptrace(req, tid, addr as *mut libc::c_void, data as *mut libc::c_void) }
}

fn wait(tid: i32, flags: libc::c_int) -> Option<(i32, libc::c_int)> {
    let mut status = 0;
    let r = unsafe { libc::waitpid(tid, &mut status, flags | libc::__WALL) };
    (r > 0).then_some((r, status))
}

fn is_event_stop(status: libc::c_int) -> bool {
    libc::WIFSTOPPED(status) && (status >> 16) == libc::PTRACE_EVENT_STOP
}

fn set_debugreg(tid: i32, n: usize, value: u64) -> bool {
    ptrace(libc::PTRACE_POKEUSER, tid, DEBUGREG + n * 8, value as usize) == 0
}

fn debugreg(tid: i32, n: usize) -> u64 {
    ptrace(libc::PTRACE_PEEKUSER, tid, DEBUGREG + n * 8, 0) as u64
}

impl Tracer {
    pub fn attach(pid: u32) -> io::Result<Self> {
        let tids: Vec<i32> = fs::read_dir(format!("/proc/{pid}/task"))?
            .filter_map(|e| e.ok()?.file_name().to_str()?.parse().ok())
            .filter(|&tid| ptrace(libc::PTRACE_SEIZE, tid, 0, 0) == 0)
            .collect();
        if tids.is_empty() {
            return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
        }
        Ok(Self { tids, parked: HashSet::new() })
    }

    /// Stops one thread. Signals that arrive meanwhile are passed on to it.
    fn stop(&self, tid: i32) -> bool {
        if ptrace(libc::PTRACE_INTERRUPT, tid, 0, 0) != 0 {
            return false;
        }
        loop {
            match wait(tid, 0) {
                Some((_, st)) if is_event_stop(st) => return true,
                Some((_, st)) if libc::WIFSTOPPED(st) => {
                    let sig = libc::WSTOPSIG(st);
                    if sig == libc::SIGTRAP && debugreg(tid, 6) & DR6_HITS != 0 {
                        // Our own breakpoint: never pass it on to the game.
                        set_debugreg(tid, 6, 0);
                        set_debugreg(tid, 7, 0);
                        ptrace(libc::PTRACE_CONT, tid, 0, 0);
                    } else {
                        ptrace(libc::PTRACE_CONT, tid, 0, sig as usize);
                    }
                }
                _ => return false,
            }
        }
    }

    /// Sets breakpoint 0 on every thread.
    pub fn arm(&mut self, addr: u64, dr7: u64) -> usize {
        self.arm_slots(&[addr], dr7)
    }

    /// Execute breakpoints on up to 4 instructions at once (the CPU has 4 slots); a hit's
    /// `slot` is the instruction's index.
    pub fn arm_execute(&mut self, instrs: &[u64]) -> usize {
        let dr7 = (0..instrs.len().min(4)).fold(0, |dr7, n| dr7 | DR7_EXECUTE << (2 * n));
        self.arm_slots(instrs, dr7)
    }

    /// Breakpoints on up to 4 addresses with a DR7 of the caller's (data watchpoints of mixed
    /// sizes).
    pub fn arm_slots(&mut self, addrs: &[u64], dr7: u64) -> usize {
        let tids = std::mem::take(&mut self.tids);
        for tid in tids {
            let set = |tid| addrs.iter().take(4).enumerate().all(|(n, &a)| set_debugreg(tid, n, a));
            if self.stop(tid) && set(tid) && set_debugreg(tid, 6, 0) && set_debugreg(tid, 7, dr7) {
                ptrace(libc::PTRACE_CONT, tid, 0, 0);
                self.tids.push(tid);
            } else {
                ptrace(libc::PTRACE_DETACH, tid, 0, 0);
            }
        }
        self.tids.len()
    }

    /// Runs the game until `timeout`, calling `on_hit` for each breakpoint hit.
    /// When `on_hit` returns false, the thread stays stopped and waiting ends.
    pub fn watch(&mut self, timeout: Duration, on_hit: impl FnMut(&Hit) -> bool) {
        let start = Instant::now();
        self.watch_until(|| start.elapsed() >= timeout, on_hit)
    }

    /// Lets the game run, calling `on_hit` at every breakpoint hit (false = stop), until `done`
    /// or the game's threads are gone.
    pub fn watch_until(&mut self, mut done: impl FnMut() -> bool, mut on_hit: impl FnMut(&Hit) -> bool) {
        while !done() && !self.tids.is_empty() {
            let Some((tid, st)) = wait(-1, libc::WNOHANG) else {
                child_stopped(Duration::from_millis(5));
                continue;
            };
            if libc::WIFEXITED(st) || libc::WIFSIGNALED(st) {
                self.tids.retain(|&t| t != tid);
                continue;
            }
            if !libc::WIFSTOPPED(st) {
                continue;
            }
            if is_event_stop(st) {
                ptrace(libc::PTRACE_CONT, tid, 0, 0);
                continue;
            }
            let sig = libc::WSTOPSIG(st);
            let dr6 = if sig == libc::SIGTRAP { debugreg(tid, 6) & DR6_HITS } else { 0 };
            if dr6 == 0 {
                ptrace(libc::PTRACE_CONT, tid, 0, sig as usize);
                continue;
            }
            set_debugreg(tid, 6, 0);
            let mut r: libc::user_regs_struct = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
            ptrace(libc::PTRACE_GETREGS, tid, 0, &mut r as *mut libc::user_regs_struct as usize);
            let gpr = [r.rax, r.rcx, r.rdx, r.rbx, r.rsp, r.rbp, r.rsi, r.rdi, r.r8, r.r9, r.r10, r.r11, r.r12, r.r13, r.r14, r.r15];
            // A 32-bit Windows game under Wine runs in a 32-bit code segment, even inside a
            // 64-bit process.
            let regs = Regs { gpr, rip: r.rip, is64: r.cs == 0x33 };
            if !on_hit(&Hit { regs, slot: dr6.trailing_zeros() as usize }) {
                self.parked.insert(tid);
                return;
            }
            ptrace(libc::PTRACE_CONT, tid, 0, 0);
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for Tracer {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        for &tid in &self.tids {
            if self.parked.contains(&tid) || self.stop(tid) {
                set_debugreg(tid, 7, 0);
                for n in 0..4 {
                    set_debugreg(tid, n, 0);
                }
                ptrace(libc::PTRACE_DETACH, tid, 0, 0);
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Waits until a traced thread stops (SIGCHLD) or `most` passes. Every signal the game gets
/// while traced stops its thread until the helper passes it on: Minecraft Dungeons (Proton)
/// raises ~900 SIGILL a second on one thread and hundreds of SIGSYS (Wine's system calls) on
/// others, and polling every 1 ms held each of them up to a millisecond or more, so the thread
/// barely ran during a 2 s re-check and the game stuttered every 8 s. SIGCHLD is blocked in
/// every thread of the helper from the start (`block_signals`), so it waits here, pending.
fn child_stopped(most: Duration) {
    unsafe {
        let mut set: libc::sigset_t = std::mem::zeroed();
        libc::sigemptyset(&mut set);
        libc::sigaddset(&mut set, libc::SIGCHLD);
        let ts = libc::timespec { tv_sec: most.as_secs() as libc::time_t, tv_nsec: most.subsec_nanos() as libc::c_long };
        libc::sigtimedwait(&set, std::ptr::null_mut(), &ts);
    }
}

/// Blocks SIGCHLD in the calling thread and every thread it starts later, for `child_stopped`:
/// call before any other thread starts (a thread not blocking it would take it and drop it).
pub fn block_sigchld() {
    unsafe {
        let mut set: libc::sigset_t = std::mem::zeroed();
        libc::sigemptyset(&mut set);
        libc::sigaddset(&mut set, libc::SIGCHLD);
        libc::pthread_sigmask(libc::SIG_BLOCK, &set, std::ptr::null_mut());
    }
}
```

`helper/src/trace_windows.rs`:

```rs
// The tracer on Windows: the helper attaches as the game's debugger (DebugActiveProcess) for
// as long as a trace runs, sets the debug registers of every thread, and takes the
// single-step exceptions they raise. Everything else the game raises goes back to the game.
// Like ptrace, debugging belongs to the thread that attached: a Tracer is made, used and
// dropped on one thread.

use std::io;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use super::{Hit, Regs, DR6_HITS, DR7_EXECUTE};
use crate::win32::*;

pub struct Tracer {
    pid: u32,
    /// A 32-bit game (its code raises STATUS_WX86_SINGLE_STEP; registers through WOW64).
    wow64: bool,
    tids: Vec<u32>,
    /// A hit `on_hit` said to stop at: the game stays frozen at it until the Tracer goes.
    parked: Option<u32>,
    gone: bool,
}

const ACCESS: u32 = THREAD_GET_CONTEXT | THREAD_SET_CONTEXT | THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME | THREAD_QUERY_INFORMATION;
/// EFLAGS' resume flag: the instruction an execute breakpoint stopped at runs once without it
/// firing again.
const RF: u32 = 1 << 16;

fn thread(tid: u32) -> Option<Handle> {
    Handle::valid(unsafe { OpenThread(ACCESS, 0, tid) })
}

fn threads_of(pid: u32) -> Vec<u32> {
    let Some(snap) = Handle::valid(unsafe { CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD, 0) }) else { return Vec::new() };
    let mut tids = Vec::new();
    let mut e: THREADENTRY32 = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    e.dwSize = std::mem::size_of::<THREADENTRY32>() as u32;
    let mut ok = unsafe { Thread32First(snap.0, &mut e) } != 0;
    while ok {
        if e.th32OwnerProcessID == pid {
            tids.push(e.th32ThreadID);
        }
        ok = unsafe { Thread32Next(snap.0, &mut e) } != 0;
    }
    tids
}

/// Sets a thread's debug registers (it must be stopped: suspended, or frozen at an event).
fn set_debug(t: &Handle, addrs: &[u64], dr7: u64) -> bool {
    let mut c = CONTEXT::new(CONTEXT_DEBUG_REGISTERS);
    if unsafe { GetThreadContext(t.0, &mut *c) } == 0 {
        return false;
    }
    for n in 0..4 {
        c.set_u64(CTX_DR[n], addrs.get(n).copied().unwrap_or(0));
    }
    c.set_u64(CTX_DR6, 0);
    c.set_u64(CTX_DR7, dr7);
    unsafe { SetThreadContext(t.0, &*c) != 0 }
}

fn continue_event(pid: u32, tid: u32, status: u32) {
    unsafe { ContinueDebugEvent(pid, tid, status) };
}

/// The next debug event, waiting at most `wait`.
fn next_event(wait: Duration) -> Option<DEBUG_EVENT> {
    let mut ev: DEBUG_EVENT = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
    (unsafe { WaitForDebugEvent(&mut ev, wait.as_millis() as u32) } != 0).then_some(ev)
}

impl Tracer {
    pub fn attach(pid: u32) -> io::Result<Self> {
        let wow64 = crate::os::is_wow64(pid);
        if unsafe { DebugActiveProcess(pid) } == 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
        }
        // The helper ending (or being ended) must never take the game with it.
        unsafe { DebugSetProcessKillOnExit(0) };
        let mut t = Tracer { pid, wow64, tids: Vec::new(), parked: None, gone: false };
        // Attaching sends the process's, its threads' and its modules' creation, then a
        // breakpoint in a thread Windows starts for it: everything up to that is let through.
        let start = Instant::now();
        while start.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(5) {
            let Some(ev) = next_event(Duration::from_millis(100)) else { continue };
            let mut status = DBG_CONTINUE;
            let mut done = false;
            match ev.dwDebugEventCode {
                CREATE_PROCESS_DEBUG_EVENT | LOAD_DLL_DEBUG_EVENT => {
                    if !ev.file_handle().is_null() {
                        unsafe { CloseHandle(ev.file_handle()) };
                    }
                }
                EXCEPTION_DEBUG_EVENT => match ev.exception_code() {
                    EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT | STATUS_WX86_BREAKPOINT => done = true,
                    _ => status = DBG_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED,
                },
                EXIT_PROCESS_DEBUG_EVENT => {
                    t.gone = true;
                    done = true;
                }
                _ => {}
            }
            continue_event(ev.dwProcessId, ev.dwThreadId, status);
            if done {
                break;
            }
        }
        t.tids = threads_of(pid);
        if t.tids.is_empty() || t.gone {
            return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, "the game has no threads"));
        }
        Ok(t)
    }

    /// Sets breakpoint 0 on every thread.
    pub fn arm(&mut self, addr: u64, dr7: u64) -> usize {
        self.arm_slots(&[addr], dr7)
    }

    /// Execute breakpoints on up to 4 instructions at once (the CPU has 4 slots); a hit's
    /// `slot` is the instruction's index.
    pub fn arm_execute(&mut self, instrs: &[u64]) -> usize {
        let dr7 = (0..instrs.len().min(4)).fold(0, |dr7, n| dr7 | DR7_EXECUTE << (2 * n));
        self.arm_slots(instrs, dr7)
    }

    /// Breakpoints on up to 4 addresses with a DR7 of the caller's (data watchpoints of mixed
    /// sizes).
    pub fn arm_slots(&mut self, addrs: &[u64], dr7: u64) -> usize {
        let addrs: Vec<u64> = addrs.iter().take(4).copied().collect();
        self.tids.retain(|&tid| {
            let Some(t) = thread(tid) else { return false };
            if unsafe { SuspendThread(t.0) } == u32::MAX {
                return false;
            }
            let ok = set_debug(&t, &addrs, dr7);
            unsafe { ResumeThread(t.0) };
            ok
        });
        self.tids.len()
    }

    /// Runs the game until `timeout`, calling `on_hit` for each breakpoint hit.
    /// When `on_hit` returns false, the thread stays stopped and waiting ends.
    pub fn watch(&mut self, timeout: Duration, on_hit: impl FnMut(&Hit) -> bool) {
        let start = Instant::now();
        self.watch_until(|| start.elapsed() >= timeout, on_hit)
    }

    /// Lets the game run, calling `on_hit` at every breakpoint hit (false = stop), until `done`
    /// or the game is gone.
    pub fn watch_until(&mut self, mut done: impl FnMut() -> bool, mut on_hit: impl FnMut(&Hit) -> bool) {
        while !done() && !self.gone && self.parked.is_none() {
            let Some(ev) = next_event(Duration::from_millis(5)) else { continue };
            let (pid, tid) = (ev.dwProcessId, ev.dwThreadId);
            match ev.dwDebugEventCode {
                CREATE_PROCESS_DEBUG_EVENT | LOAD_DLL_DEBUG_EVENT => {
                    if !ev.file_handle().is_null() {
                        unsafe { CloseHandle(ev.file_handle()) };
                    }
                    continue_event(pid, tid, DBG_CONTINUE);
                }
                EXIT_PROCESS_DEBUG_EVENT => {
                    self.gone = true;
                    continue_event(pid, tid, DBG_CONTINUE);
                }
                EXIT_THREAD_DEBUG_EVENT => {
                    self.tids.retain(|&t| t != tid);
                    continue_event(pid, tid, DBG_CONTINUE);
                }
                EXCEPTION_DEBUG_EVENT => {
                    let code = ev.exception_code();
                    if code != EXCEPTION_SINGLE_STEP && code != STATUS_WX86_SINGLE_STEP {
                        // The game's own exceptions (C++ exceptions, its own breakpoints, faults it
                        // handles) go back to it.
                        continue_event(pid, tid, DBG_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED);
                        continue;
                    }
                    match self.take_hit(tid, code) {
                        Some(hit) => {
                            if !on_hit(&hit) {
                                self.parked = Some(tid);
                                return;
                            }
                            continue_event(pid, tid, DBG_CONTINUE);
                        }
                        // A single step with no breakpoint in DR6: one of ours whose DR6 was
                        // cleared when the breakpoints were set again (Drop's comment). Games
                        // don't single-step themselves; passing it on would end the game.
                        None => continue_event(pid, tid, DBG_CONTINUE),
                    }
                }
                _ => continue_event(pid, tid, DBG_CONTINUE),
            }
        }
    }

    /// A single step at `tid`: one of ours when DR6 says a breakpoint fired. Clears DR6 and,
    /// for an execute breakpoint, sets RF so the instruction runs on.
    fn take_hit(&self, tid: u32, code: u32) -> Option<Hit> {
        let t = thread(tid)?;
        let mut d = CONTEXT::new(CONTEXT_DEBUG_REGISTERS);
        if unsafe { GetThreadContext(t.0, &mut *d) } == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let dr6 = d.u64_at(CTX_DR6) & DR6_HITS;
        if dr6 == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let slot = dr6.trailing_zeros() as usize;
        let execute = (d.u64_at(CTX_DR7) >> (16 + 4 * slot)) & 3 == 0;
        d.set_u64(CTX_DR6, 0);
        unsafe { SetThreadContext(t.0, &*d) };
        let mut gpr = [0u64; 16];
        let regs = if self.wow64 && code == STATUS_WX86_SINGLE_STEP {
            let mut w = WOW64_CONTEXT::new(WOW64_CONTEXT_CONTROL | WOW64_CONTEXT_INTEGER);
            if unsafe { Wow64GetThreadContext(t.0, &mut *w) } == 0 {
                return None;
            }
            for (n, off) in WOW_GPR.iter().enumerate() {
                gpr[n] = w.u32_at(*off) as u64;
            }
            if execute {
                w.set_u32(0, WOW64_CONTEXT_CONTROL);
                w.set_u32(WOW_EFLAGS, w.u32_at(WOW_EFLAGS) | RF);
                unsafe { Wow64SetThreadContext(t.0, &*w) };
            }
            Regs { gpr, rip: w.u32_at(WOW_EIP) as u64, is64: false }
        } else {
            let mut c = CONTEXT::new(CONTEXT_CONTROL | CONTEXT_INTEGER);
            if unsafe { GetThreadContext(t.0, &mut *c) } == 0 {
                return None;
            }
            for (n, off) in CTX_GPR.iter().enumerate() {
                gpr[n] = c.u64_at(*off);
            }
            if execute {
                c.set_u32(0x30, CONTEXT_CONTROL);
                c.set_u32(CTX_EFLAGS, c.u32_at(CTX_EFLAGS) | RF);
                unsafe { SetThreadContext(t.0, &*c) };
            }
            Regs { gpr, rip: c.u64_at(CTX_RIP), is64: true }
        };
        Some(Hit { regs, slot })
    }
}

impl Drop for Tracer {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if !self.gone {
            // Clear every thread's breakpoints, then let through what is still queued. Every
            // single step is ours: a thread whose hit was on its way when its registers were
            // cleared (DR6 with them) can't be told apart, and handing it to the game kills it
            // (EXCEPTION_SINGLE_STEP, unhandled: it happened to the stand-in under load). A
            // hit can take a while to arrive in a busy game, so the queue is waited on until
            // it stays empty for 100 ms.
            self.arm_slots(&[], 0);
            if let Some(tid) = self.parked.take() {
                continue_event(self.pid, tid, DBG_CONTINUE);
            }
            while let Some(ev) = next_event(Duration::from_millis(100)) {
                let status = match ev.dwDebugEventCode {
                    CREATE_PROCESS_DEBUG_EVENT | LOAD_DLL_DEBUG_EVENT => {
                        if !ev.file_handle().is_null() {
                            unsafe { CloseHandle(ev.file_handle()) };
                        }
                        DBG_CONTINUE
                    }
                    EXCEPTION_DEBUG_EVENT => match ev.exception_code() {
                        EXCEPTION_SINGLE_STEP | STATUS_WX86_SINGLE_STEP => {
                            self.take_hit(ev.dwThreadId, ev.exception_code());
                            DBG_CONTINUE
                        }
                        _ => DBG_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED,
```
